Additionally, it also looks at the scalability of CNCs production, identifying key challenges and discussing potential future industrial applications for a better understanding of the scope, contribution, selectivity, and applicability of these advanced materials. Finally, this study provides a comprehensive analysis of CNCs as a sustainable and high-performance reinforcement for biopolymer-based composites. Unlike earlier reviews, this work connects extraction, modification, and application strategies, providing an integrated perspective on both laboratory research and piloting implementation. Additionally, it highlights the potential application of CNC-based biocomposites in various industrial, engineering, and biomedical sectors as an eco-friendly alternative to hazardous fossil-based materials. Applications include industrial wastewater treatment, bioplastics, biocomposites, nanocatalysts manufacturing, biomedical tool preparation, medicinal dosage formulation, packaging material production, and other environmentally friendly engineering products. The goal is to achieve triple benefits, encompassing environmental, economic, and agro-industrial aspects, by advancing cutting-edge research for the next generation. Graphical abstract

title: Enhancing the Performance of PBAT Composites via Incorporation of Nano TiO_2-Tannic Acid Hybrid Filler
author: Lv, Chang
journal: Journal of Polymers and the Environment
abstract: Nano-TiO_2 improved the interfacial compatibility of PBAT with TA. TA enhanced the antibacterial activity of PBAT/TiO_2 under UV-free irritation. The mechanical properties and enzymatic degradation of PBAT/TiTA were enhanced. In the post-pandemic era, biodegradable materials with antibacterial properties effectively meet safety needs for protective applications. However, although tannic acid (TA) has excellent antimicrobial properties, its abundant phenolic hydroxyl groups make it uneven dispersion in the polymer matrix. In this study, nano-TiO_2-TA (TiTA) hybrid filler was prepared firstly and then mixed with poly (butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) (PBAT/TiTA) via melt blending. Notably, TiTA hybrid filler not only enhanced the degradability and mechanical properties of PBAT, but also endowed strong antibacterial activity with Ultraviolet (UV)-free irradiation, which overcome the limitation of UV irradiation to the antibacterial activity of TiO_2. When the TiTA content was 7.5 wt%, the comprehensive performance of the composite was optimal. This work provides a simple strategy to address the dispersion of TA and to develop TiO_2-based antibacterial materials with UV-free irradiation. The resulting antibacterial biodegradable composites holds great promise for applications in medical and food packaging fields. Graphical abstract

title: Radiation-shielding concrete systems: an analytical review of material strategies, shielding efficiency, and engineering performance
author: Owais, Mahmoud
abstract: Radiation-shielding concrete (RSC) is widely used in nuclear, medical, and industrial facilities because it combines structural functionality with the ability to attenuate ionizing radiation. This review provides an integrated analysis of the main material strategies used in RSC, with emphasis on the relationships among material composition, shielding efficiency, mechanical performance, and thermal stability. Unlike previous studies that focused on isolated material classes or single performance aspects, the present review synthesizes conventional heavyweight aggregate systems, sustainable and waste-derived concretes, nanomaterial-modified mixtures, fiber-reinforced formulations, and the influence of elevated temperature within a unified analytical framework. To support this analysis, a structured literature database was developed from a screened subset of experimental studies selected from a broader literature survey. Studies were included in the quantitative synthesis when they reported original experimental data on radiation-shielding concrete and provided sufficiently extractable information on mixture composition, density, exposure conditions, shielding response, and/or mechanical properties. This screening process yielded 382 analyzable mix/specimen records from 24 source studies, described by 19 variables covering mixture composition, additives, exposure conditions, shielding indicators, and engineering properties. Shielding performance was evaluated using key parameters, including the linear attenuation coefficient (LAC), mass attenuation coefficient (MAC), half-value layer (HVL), tenth-value layer (TVL), mean free path (MFP), and radiation protection efficiency (RPE). The findings confirm that attenuation efficiency is governed primarily by density, elemental and mineralogical composition, concrete thickness, and radiation energy. Comparative analysis shows that heavyweight aggregate systems generally provide superior gamma-ray shielding compared with ordinary concrete, as reflected by higher LAC values and lower HVL, TVL, and MFP values. Within the compiled evidence, magnetite- and barite-based concretes show the strongest overall gamma-ray attenuation potential, hematite-containing systems provide a favorable balance between shielding efficiency and mechanical strength, and slag-based concretes offer competitive attenuation performance together with sustainability benefits. However, the relative ranking of these systems depends on photon energy, mixture design, aggregate mineralogy, and the required balance between shielding effectiveness, workability, strength, durability, and thermal stability. Sustainable and modified systems, including recycled aggregates, steel slag, CRT glass, nanomaterials, and fibers, show promising potential for combining shielding capability with improved environmental performance, although their long-term durability and elevated-temperature behavior remain insufficiently standardized. Overall, this review provides an evidence-based understanding of current RSC development and identifies future directions for designing high-performance, durable, and sustainable shielding concrete systems.

title: Implantable flexible neuroelectrodes: advances in material innovation, structural design, and performance optimization
author: Su, Jiaqi
abstract: In recent years, implantable neuroelectrodes have been widely applied in various fields, including deep brain electrical stimulation, neuroprosthesis, and recording neuronal electrical activity in neuroscience research. However, with the rapid advancement of neuroscience and brain–computer interface technology, the limitations of traditional rigid neuroelectrodes have become increasingly evident. Flexible neuroelectrodes constructed from soft materials are emerging as a key research focus in the neural interface field. This review presents a systematic classification of the material selection, structural design, and key performance of implantable flexible neuroelectrodes and analyzes the optimization of achieving electrode flexibility in avoiding tissue damage and immune response. Furthermore, we summarized the contemporary challenges in performance optimization and material innovation, proposing potential solutions. By integrating and reviewing existing innovative approaches to flexible implantable neuroelectrodes, this review aims to provide an important theoretical foundation and technical guidance for the development of high-performance implantable neuroelectrodes. 目 的 近年来, 基于软材料构建的柔性神经电极正成为神经接口领域的重要研究方向。 通过整合并评述现有柔性植入式神经电极的创新方法, 本文旨在为高性能植入式神经电极的发展提供重要的理论基础与技术指导。 创新点 本文构建了一个 “材料选择-结构设计-性能优化” 的多维度研究框架, 以解决神经接口的长期可靠性难题。 方 法 1. 在材料层面, 本文对柔性导电材料进行了系统分类, 并评估了其内在物理与化学特性, 以实现与神经组织的力学匹配。 2. 在结构层面, 本文回顾了一维、 二维和三维构型下的神经微电极工程, 以优化组织整合。 3. 在性能方面, 本文聚焦于两大核心支柱: 其一涉及高保真记录与安全刺激所需的电学特性, 其二则围绕长期稳定性策略 (例如生物相容性涂层), 以确保在严苛生理环境中的可靠性。 结 论 通过整合材料选择、 结构设计和性能优化, 本综述为克服当前柔性神经电极的瓶颈、 实现稳定长期的神经假体功能提供了方向。

title: Methods of removing deposits in oil and gas pipelines: a review
author: Karimi, Mohammad
abstract: Deposition in the oil, gas, and petrochemical industries occurs mainly due to the passage of water, organic deposits, and corrosion products in hydrocarbon pipelines. The composition of deposits in oil and gas pipelines differs at different points and routes. Especially, deposition in long-distance transmission lines is often due to mineral and organic deposits. Variable environmental conditions such as the mixed fluid types in pipelines, pressure, temperature, pH, hydrocarbon type, and pipe material can accelerate the deposition process. Consequently, these variations reduce effective pipe diameter and increase destructive corrosion factors and microbiological phenomena. Chemical methods with special inhibitors and suitable solvents are a common method for removing these deposits. Moreover, phosphonate and polycarboxylate inhibitors are consumed for removing mineral deposits, and aromatic solvents and surfactants for organic deposits. Mechanical methods, e.g., pigging, have become a fully cost-effective method in long-distance pipelines. Recently, new methods such as nano-coatings and superhydrophobic coatings on the pipe wall and electromagnetic or ultrasonic systems to create vibrations and destroy mineral deposits growing in the pipe have been considered low-cost solutions in some places. In this analytical review study, considering Iranian diverse climatic conditions, combined solutions with modern technologies were selected as the best approach for managing deposition and corrosion and were introduced as solutions to advance productivity. Graphical Abstract

title: Forward osmosis in the modern era: recent progress in membrane engineering and draw solute
author: Lohar, Ajay
abstract: The escalating global demand for clean water, driven by population growth, climate change, and rapid industrialization, has intensified the need for energy-efficient and sustainable water treatment technologies. Forward osmosis (FO) has emerged as a promising membrane-based separation process owing to its low or near-zero pressure requirement, reduced energy consumption, and lower fouling propensity compared to conventional pressure-driven processes such as reverse osmosis. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent progress in forward osmosis, with particular emphasis on advancements in membrane engineering and the development of innovative draw solutes. The fundamental principles governing FO, including osmotic pressure, membrane characteristics, and concentration polarization phenomena, are systematically discussed. Recent developments in FO membranes ranging from conventional asymmetric and thin-film composite membranes to nanofiltration-based and functionalized membranes—are critically analyzed in terms of structure, performance, and material selection. In parallel, the review presents an in-depth classification and evaluation of draw solutes, including inorganic salts, organic compounds, fertilizers, nanoparticles, hydrogels, dendrimers, ionic liquids, and deep eutectic solvents, highlighting their osmotic performance, reverse solute flux, regeneration strategies, and practical limitations. Special attention is given to emerging green and responsive draw solutes that offer improved sustainability and recovery efficiency. Finally, current challenges and future research directions are outlined, focusing on mitigating concentration polarization, reducing reverse solute flux, and expanding FO applications beyond desalination to areas such as wastewater treatment, resource recovery, and product concentration. This review aims to serve as a useful reference for researchers and engineers working toward the large-scale implementation of forward osmosis technology.

title: Turning E-waste into water treatment: preliminary physicochemical and diffusion‑based ion‑transport assessment of cationic cellulose acetate-based membranes
author: Silva, Mayara Teixeira
abstract: Water pollution by heavy metals poses serious environmental and public health risks, driving the need for cost‑effective and sustainable treatment technologies. This study explores the fabrication and performance of novel ion‑exchange membranes (IEMs) based on cellulose acetate (CA) blended waste keyboard particles. Three membrane types were produced: MStd (CA), MR (CA and cationic resin) and MKey (CA and keyboard particles), and each was tested with and without HCl activation. Physicochemical characterization included hydraulic permeability, water uptake, porosity, drop contact angle, ion exchange capacity (IEC), FTIR, and SEM analyses. Results showed that both MR and MKey membranes exhibited significantly higher permeability and IEC compared to MStd, while porosity and water uptake remained similar, indicating effective structural blending. Contact angles confirmed hydrophilicity across all samples, and FTIR/SEM data demonstrated that acid activation did not alter membrane morphology or surface functional groups. In diffusion tests using a copper chloride solution (1200 ppm), acid-activated MR and MKey reached concentration equilibrium more rapidly (180–240 min) than their non-activated counterparts, highlighting improved ion-transport kinetics. These results demonstrate the feasibility of incorporating keyboard‑derived residues into cellulose acetate membranes and indicate promising diffusion‑based ion‑transport behavior. Graphical abstract

title: Research on environmentally friendly temperature-resistant and salt-resistant high polymeric stability graft-modified cellulose filtrate reducer
author: Li, Yana
abstract: To develop an environmentally friendly filtrate reducer that is resistant to high temperatures and salt and exhibits high stability, this study utilized natural cotton chemically modified to prepare sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC-Na). Then, N-vinylpyrrolidone was graft-polymerized onto CMC-Na to synthesize graft-modified carboxymethyl cellulose (g-CMC). The products were characterized via Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and polarized optical microscopy (POM). SEM, XRD, and POM results indicated carboxymethylation and graft modification changed cellulose microstructure, lowered crystallinity, and raised specific surface area. The response surface methodology was employed to optimize the alkalization and etherification conditions, while single-factor experiments determined that a urea dosage of 6 wt% and a water-to-cotton ratio of 4 resulted in a maximum degree of substitution of 1.21 for g-CMC. Rheological and filtration performance evaluations indicated that the optimal dosage of g-CMC as a filtrate reducer in drilling fluid was 1.5 wt%. After aging at 160 ℃ for 96 h, the filtration volume of the g-CMC-based drilling fluid showed no significant increase compared to its pre-aging performance. Furthermore, with 30 wt% sodium chloride added, the filtration volume of g-CMC drilling fluid at normal temperature and pressure is 9.97 mL and an apparent viscosity (AV) of 46.2 mPa·s, meeting the relevant performance standards. Compared with commercially available cellulose, resin, and other filtrate reducers, g-CMC exhibits superior filtration performance and favorable compatibility with conventional drilling fluid additives. Therefore, g-CMC is demonstrated to be an environmentally friendly filtrate reducer with excellent heat resistance, salt tolerance, and high colloidal stability.

title: Recycled High-Density Polyethylene as a Sustainable Wood Alternative for Indoor Furniture
author: Elkholy, Mostafa
abstract: The growing volume of plastic waste and the scarcity of timber have made alternative materials for use in interior furniture attractive. The aim of this study is to assess the feasibility of using recycled high-density polyethylene (HDPE) as an alternative to wood-based materials. The cleaned and shredded post-consumer HDPE waste was compression molded at 200–210 °C to form flat panels. Mechanical properties were determined by tensile testing, while moisture resistance was determined by water adsorption testing. The recycled HDPE had tensile strength values up to 22.86 MPa and very low water adsorption ( ≈ < 0.01%) compared to the conventional medium-density fiberboard (MDF). The feasibility of production was performed through a techno-economic analysis, resulting in an internal rate of return (IRR) of 45.3% and a positive net present value (NPV) in five years. These findings indicate that it is possible to have a significant potential for recycled HDPE components for small-scale manufacture in the furniture industry. This study does not have detailed polymer characterization, long-term durability, data, and environmental assessment of life cycles. Overall, recycled HDPE presents a potential sustainable material, but further research is necessary to evaluate its structural and environmental properties.

title: Evolution of oil spill remediation technologies from conventional to emerging solutions
author: Amoako, Christian
abstract: Oil spills pose significant environmental and socioeconomic challenges in marine and terrestrial ecosystems, where petroleum hydrocarbons can adversely affect aquatic organisms, coastal habitats, and farmland food products. This review provides an evolutionary overview of oil spill remediation technologies, from conventional approaches, including mechanical, thermal, chemical, and biological methods, with emphasis on their operational principles, effectiveness, advantages, and environmental limitations, to emerging precision-based bioremediation, including omics-based biosurfactant remediation, biosurfactant-enhanced bioremediation, and engineered microbial consortia bioremediation. Particular attention is given to the role of hydrocarbonoclastic microorganisms in petroleum biodegradation, highlighting the mechanisms of microbial hydrocarbon utilization and degradation. Graphical Abstract

title: Microwave-initiated turpentine polymerization for multifunctional rubberwood modification: integrated antibacterial, superhydrophobic, and termite-resistant properties
author: Wang, Hailun
abstract: Turpentine oil (TO) has attracted considerable interest as a promising wood preservative due to its antifungal properties, biodegradability, and low toxicity to vertebrates. However, its high volatility limits its application as a wood preservative. To resolve this problem, FeCl_3 was employed as a Lewis acid catalyst to initiate the cationic polymerization of α-pinene, forming a self-encapsulated poly-α-pinene system. The research results demonstrated that the water contact angle of poly-turpentine oil (Poly-TO) modified rubberwood increased from 82.34° to 117.41°. The rubberwood Poly-TO treated achieved an acceptable decay resistance rating and could satisfy the requirements on class I defined in Chinese standard GB/T 13942.1 (2009). Compared with the untreated wood, the mass loss reduced from 47.23 to 9.13% and from 37.40 to 8.34%, respectively, after 12 weeks’ exposure to white and brown rot fungi under 28 °C and 85% relative humidity storage conditions. Microstructure analysis proved Poly-TO treatment can protect internal structure of wood. The Poly-TO treated rubberwood also showed significantly improvement on termite resistance. Compared with the wood untreated, the mass loss reduced from 8.73 to 0.94%. The results indicate that Poly-TO as a wood preservative showed promise. Graphical abstract

title: Structure and Morphology of Electrospun Polycaprolactone Fibers Loaded with Silver Nanoparticles Formed in the Presence of β-Cyclodextrin
author: Riabov, S. V.
abstract: Polymer microfibres (polymer mats) based on polycaprolactone and filled with metallic silver nanoparticles were obtained by electrospinning. Ascorbic acid was used as a reducing agent for Ag^+ ions, either individually or in combination with the naturally occurring macrocyclic compound β-cyclodextrin (β-CD), which also stabilizes for Ag^0 nanoparticles. The presence of Ag^0 nanoparticles in the fibres was confirmed by UV spectroscopy, X-ray phase analysis method, and transmission electron microscopy. It has been shown that the use of β-CD during the reduction of Ag^+ ions allows smaller silver crystallites to be obtained, while also resulting in decreased thermal stability of the material. This material can be used for the development of biocompatible composites with an antibacterial activity for a medical applications.

title: Time-Resolved Investigation of the Priming Effect of Biodegradable Plastics on Soil Organic Matter Using Radiocarbon Analysis
author: Ju, Sungbin
journal: Journal of Polymers and the Environment
abstract: As biodegradable plastics become integrated into the modern economy, soil contamination by biodegradable microplastics (MPs) has raised concerns owing to their potential to alter soil organic matter (SOM), an important carbon reservoir, through priming effects. Priming effects refer to the acceleration (positive) or suppression (negative) of SOM decomposition following an external carbon input. Previous studies have relied on carbon-13 isotope analysis, which lacks the resolution required for precise carbon tracing, to study the priming effects of biodegradable MPs. Herein we present a novel approach combining accelerator mass spectrometry-based radiocarbon (carbon-14) analysis with a closed-jar incubation system to quantify the priming effects of two fossil-based biodegradable MPs, poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) and poly(butylene adipate- co -terephthalate) (PBAT). This method enables high-resolution time-resolved partitioning of biogenic and fossil-derived carbon sources. Both biodegradable MPs show a net negative priming effect (up to − 35.4 µg C g^− 1 soil for PCL after 9 d, and − 9.6 µg C g^− 1 soil for PBAT after 24 d), with transient positive priming observed at certain time points. This study provides a robust approach for accurate assessment of the priming effects of biodegradable plastics on SOM and offers a potential analytical framework to devise end-of-life management strategies for biodegradable plastics in agroecosystems.

title: Genetic and morphological variation in taxonomically critical populations of Quercus petraea s.l. in Southern Europe
author: Di Pietro, Romeo
abstract: This study investigated the genetic and morphological variability of critical populations of Quercus petraea s.l. in southern Europe considering taxonomic and biogeographical issues. Ten EST-SSR markers were applied on sixteen populations of Q. petraea s.l., including Q. petraea subsp. petraea , Q. petraea subsp. austrotyrrhenica , Q. dalechampii auct non Ten, and Q. banatus , to assess genetic variation within and among populations using specific indices. Genetic structure was analysed using Bayesian clustering. Eight populations of potentially interfertile white oaks such as Q. pubescens (5) and Q. robur (3) were included in the overall dataset (24 populations) for comparison. Multivariate analysis procedures were applied to analyse genetic relationships among populations. The morphological variability of oak individuals was assessed only on the Q. petraea s.l. populations based on traits observed in leaves, twigs, and acorns. The patterns of covariation between morphological traits, taxonomic identity, and the geographical distribution of sessile oak populations were also investigated. The analysis on the overall dataset revealed four main genetic clusters for Q. petraea s.l.: one of possible ancestral origin, one occurring mainly in the Balkans, one spread across southern Italy, and one distributed primarly in western and central Europe. From a morphometric perspective, only a few leaf morphological traits exhibited variation trends correlated with the genetic structure pattern. Considerable overlap was found among populations within the Q. petraea collective group from both the genetic and morphological side. The variability observed was insufficient to distinguish species other than Q. petraea (Matt.) Liebl. (i.e. Q. dalechampii auct. non Ten., Q. banatus Kučera). However, all Q. petraea s.l. populations were found to be clearly distinguishable from the Q. robur subsp. robur and Q. pubescens subsp. pubescens populations included in the dataset as outgroups.

title: Development and characterization of PBS and PBAT blend based sustainable films for food packaging applications
author: Adeebpasha, A.
abstract: The increasing environmental concern associated with non-biodegradable plastics have sparked significant interest in biodegradable alternatives such as polylactic acid (PLA), polybutylene succinate (PBS) and polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT) for food packaging applications. While these polymers show potential, their individual properties often fall short of packaging requirements. The present study showed the optimization of barrier and mechanical properties of PBS/PBAT blend. The PBS/PBAT blends exhibited composition-dependent physical interactions and partial miscibility without external compatibilizers. PBS-rich blends displayed improved mechanical strength, moisture barrier performance, and surface hydrophobicity, while increasing PBAT content influenced flexibility, UV-shielding capability, and light-transmission characteristics. The FTIR spectroscopy confirmed successful blending through shifts in characteristic absorption bands. Water contact angle analysis showed increased surface hydrophobicity with higher content of PBS. The Water Vapor Transmission Rate (WVTR) of PBAT decreased significantly with PBS incorporation, demonstrating improved barrier performance. The UV-Visible spectroscopic results revealed increased absorbance in the UV region upon blending with PBAT, indicating improved UV-blocking capacity of blends while maintaining visible transparency. Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) confirmed phase-separated morphology particularly in PBAT-rich blends. Overall, the results demonstrate that the composition of the PBS/PBAT blend can be tailored to control mechanical, barrier, and optical properties, suggesting potential applications in biodegradable packaging.

title: Asymmetric poly(ethylene glycol)-b-polylactide-b-poly(ethylene glycol) triblock copolymer micelles for dual delivery of paclitaxel and cisplatin: in vitro release, degradation, and biological evaluation
author: Li, Rongye
abstract: Recent advances in polymeric nanocarriers have highlighted the potential of amphiphilic block copolymers for the simultaneous delivery of chemotherapeutic agents with different physicochemical properties. In this study, asymmetric poly(ethylene glycol)-b-polylactide-b-poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG- b -PLA- b -PEG) triblock copolymers were synthesized via ring-opening polymerization, end-group functionalization, and click coupling, and subsequently evaluated as biodegradable nanocarriers for the co-delivery of paclitaxel (PTX) and cisplatin (CDDP). The copolymers were characterized by ^1H nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and gel permeation chromatography (GPC). Self-assembly in aqueous media yielded spherical micelles with uniform size distributions, as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and dynamic light scattering (DLS). The micelles exhibited efficient encapsulation of PTX and CDDP with high drug-loading capacities and encapsulation efficiencies. Hydrolytic degradation studies conducted at 37 °C for 45 days revealed progressive cleavage of the ester bond, reduction in molecular weight, and gradual disintegration of the micellar structure. In vitro release studies of single- and dual-drug-loaded micelles demonstrated sustained release of both drugs over time. Analysis of the release data using the Korsmeyer–Peppas model provided insight into the release behavior and suggested contributions from both diffusion and polymer degradation processes. The biocompatibility of the unloaded triblock copolymer micelles was assessed through cytocompatibility, hemocompatibility, and zebrafish embryo assays, which indicated low intrinsic toxicity and minimal hemolytic activity. Collectively, these results demonstrate that PEG- b -PLA- b -PEG triblock copolymer micelles can be recognized as biodegradable carriers capable of dual-drug encapsulation and sustained release, providing a useful platform for further investigation of combination drug delivery systems. Graphical abstract Asymmetric PEG- b -PLA- b -PEG triblock copolymers were synthesized and self-assembled into uniform micelles capable of co-encapsulating Paclitaxel and Cisplatin. The micellar architecture provided controlled degradation and synchronized dual-drug release over 45 days. The combination of tunable structure, sustained release, and excellent biocompatibility highlights these triblock copolymer micelles as efficient nanocarriers for combinational cancer therapy

title: Plastics to fertilizer: A polymer system based on isosorbide as a monomer, plasticizer, and fertilizer
author: Fujimata, Shunsuke
abstract: Plastics have long been designed as durable materials with limited consideration of their fate after use. In contrast, a polymer system that enables end-of-life plastics to no longer to be discarded but instead to be transformed into fertilizers that actively benefit ecosystems, would be very desirable indeed. Such a concept may offer a new direction for polymer design and expand the potential roles of plastic materials. In our previous studies, we demonstrated that isosorbide-based polycarbonates (PIC) can be converted into fertilizer-compatible components through ammonolysis after use. Building on this concept, the present study introduces dual-functional isosorbide-based plasticizers that simultaneously reduce the brittleness of PIC while also being convertible into fertilizer-compatible components through ammonolysis after use. The effectiveness of the degradation products obtained from this plastic system, composed of PIC and isosorbide-based plasticizers, as fertilizers was validated through the growth of both a model plant and an edible vegetable.

title: Nanoparticle-driven parameters betterment in unexplored NLCs: engineering ZLI-3103/TiO_2 systems for next-generation capacitors, sensors, and displays
author: Saxena, Saransh
abstract: Developing low-power and high-speed electro-optical devices remains a challenge due to the high operating voltages and slow switching responses of conventional liquid crystals. To overcome this limitation, this study reports the fabrication of nanostructured composites using a nematic liquid crystal (NLC) doped with silane-functionalized titanium oxide (TiO_2) nanoparticles (NPs). The explicit uniqueness of this work lies in utilizing these stable hybrids to fundamentally lower rotational viscosity ( γ ), which allows for simultaneously optimizing both switching speed and threshold voltage ( V _ th ). This targeted mechanism constitutes our main contribution, driving a simultaneous 32% faster switching response ( τ ) and a 25% lower Vth through rapid director realignment while fully preserving the host’s clearing temperature ( T _ NI ) and mesomorphic stability. Ultimately, this approach establishes TiO_2 hybrids as a highly efficient, fast-switching platform for next-generation optoelectronic displays. Graphical abstract

title: Dendrimer-Based Nanoplatforms for Cancer Diagnosis and Therapy: from Liquid Biopsy to Targeted Protein Degradation
author: Alibaglou, Mahsa Hasannejad
abstract: Dendrimers are highly branched, monodisperse macromolecules that have emerged as versatile nanoplatforms for cancer diagnosis and therapy owing to their well-defined architecture, multivalent surface functionality, and tunable physicochemical properties. Their unique structure enables the efficient loading of therapeutic agents, nucleic acids, imaging probes, and targeting ligands within a single multifunctional system, supporting the development of precision nanomedicine. This review summarizes recent advances in dendrimer-based platforms for cancer management, highlighting their applications in liquid biopsy, molecular imaging, theranostics, catalytic therapy, active drug delivery, multifunctional nanocarriers, tumor microenvironment-responsive systems, gene delivery, biomimetic nanoplatforms, cancer immunotherapy, and targeted protein degradation using proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs). Recent studies demonstrate that dendrimers can enhance drug solubility, improve pharmacokinetics, enable controlled and stimuli-responsive drug release, increase tumor accumulation, and reduce systemic toxicity. Furthermore, dendrimer-based systems have shown considerable potential to remodel the tumor microenvironment, induce immunogenic cell death, enhance immune activation, and facilitate combination therapies. Emerging strategies integrating biomimetic coatings, hydrogels, microneedle patches, and multifunctional theranostic platforms further expand their biomedical applications. Despite encouraging preclinical outcomes, challenges related to large-scale manufacturing, long-term safety, clinical translation, and regulatory approval remain. Continued advances in dendrimer engineering and multifunctional nanotechnology are expected to accelerate the development of next-generation precision nanomedicines, offering promising opportunities to improve cancer diagnosis, treatment, and patient outcomes. Graphical Abstract

title: Sulfur Passivation During Acid Leaching of Sulfide Ore: An Overview
author: Haile, Michael Girma
abstract: The problem associated with sulfur passivation remains one of the most significant factors affecting the efficiency of the sulfide ore leaching process by blocking oxidant access to mineral surfaces and limiting metal recovery. However, recent electrochemical and surface studies indicate that passivation is not a universal phenomenon but rather a regime-dependent and mineral-specific mechanism whose nature, severity, and mitigation strategy differ on the basis of leaching conditions, mineral type, and operating parameters. Drawing on a structured survey of the recent literature, this review synthesizes this emerging understanding by explicitly differentiating passivation mechanisms across atmospheric pressure leaching and high-pressure leaching regimes, integrating kinetic growth to explain sulfur layer evolution and provide a structured decision matrix to diagnose their dominant passivation mode and select targeted mitigation strategies. The critical influence of mineralogical parameters (ore mineralogy, mineral associations, galvanic interactions, gangue mineralogy, particle size, and surface area) and operational variables (temperature, pressure, oxidant type, and leaching time) on passivation morphology, density, and permeability is systematically examined. Mitigation strategies including pressure and temperature control, pH and redox potential management, surfactant and dispersant addition, and alkaline pretreatment are critically evaluated within this framework. Finally, this review identifies critical knowledge gaps and priorities for future research, bridging the fragmentation in the literature where most studies focus on isolated minerals or leaching systems. The result is a coherent analytical and practical framework for improving sulfide ore recovery efficiency through rational passivation control. Graphical Abstract

title: Scalable Reconfigurable Meta-textile System Enabling Adaptive and Self-Automated Thermoregulation
author: Sun, Ya
abstract: Radiative thermoregulatory textiles control thermal emission without continuous energy input, offering a sustainable route to personal thermal comfort and energy savings. However, it remains challenging for such textiles to autonomously respond to complex or rapid environmental changes while maintaining comfort across wide temperature fluctuations. Here, we develop a scalable, adaptive, and self-automated thermoregulatory meta-textile (ASTM) system by integrating a reconfigurable metallic–polymer meta-textile with sensing, control, and actuation modules. The mechanically reconfigurable metafiber architecture provides large and continuous infrared emissivity modulation, while the closed-loop control system enables automatic adaptation to environmental changes without human intervention. The ASTM expands the thermal comfort zone by 16.5 °C and maintains a stable temperature range of 20–26.7 °C during outdoor temperature fluctuations of up to 23.4 °C. Building energy simulations show that the meta-textile can achieve an average annual heating and cooling energy savings of 515 MJ m^−2 across global climates, with notable CO_2 reduction potential. This work demonstrates a system-integrated strategy for smart thermoregulatory textiles and provides a practical route toward personalized thermal comfort and energy-efficient building envelopes. Graphical Abstract

title: Boehmite/Polyacrylonitrile Composite Nanofiber Separator with Enhanced Ionic Conductivity and Thermal Stability for Lithium-Ion Batteries
author: Tu, Zhi-Jun
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) and polypropylene (PP) are widely used in commercial lithium-ion battery (LIB) separators owing to their high mechanical strength and chemical stability. However, both polymers suffer from poor high-temperature tolerance, low porosity, and inadequate electrolyte wettability, making it difficult to reconcile electrochemical performance with safety under thermal stress. Developing advanced lithium-ion battery separators is therefore crucial for achieving high efficiency, safe LIBs. This study presents a boehmite/polyacrylonitrile (BM/PAN) composite nanofiber separator fabricated by electrospinning and systematically examines how BM loading affects separator microstructure and electrochemical behavior. Compared with commercial PP separators, the BM/PAN composites exhibit a unique three-dimensional interconnected fiber network, together with markedly improved wettability, thermal stability and electrochemical properties. The optimal formulation contains 4 wt% BM (denoted PAN-BM-4) exhibited an outstanding wettability with electrolyte uptake of 692.5% with the porosity of 80.7% and electrolyte contact angle of 25.5°, ensuring rapid electrolyte infiltration and efficient ion transport. it also displayed a higher mechanical property with tensile strength of 7.9 MPa and elongation at break of 27% (cf. 6.5 MPa and about 45% for pure PAN), indicating enhanced structural integrity. Meanwhile, such PAN-BM-4 separator demonstrates an excellent thermal stability with negligible shrinkage at 200 °C and a residual mass of 57.6% at 800 °C, effectively mitigating the thermal-runaway risk of conventional separators. Moreover, as to the electrochemical performance, this unique PAN-BM-4 separator showed an ionic conductivity of 3.31 mS/cm, more than six times that of commercial PP, and the electrochemical stability window exceeding 5.5 V (versus Li^+/Li) and a Li^+ transference number ( t _Li+) of 0.42, substantially higher than PP (0.28) and pure PAN (0.34), reflecting enhanced selective Li+ transport. Besides, in half-cell testing, the PAN-BM-4 separator delivers an initial discharge capacity of 140.6 mAh/g at 0.5 C with 88.3% capacity retention after 100 cycles. in summary, this work establishes a viable materials-design strategy and experimental framework for next-generation LiB separators that simultaneously achieve high ionic conductivity, superior thermal stability and favorable interfacial compatibility.

title: Natural fibre reinforced concrete: a review of natural fibres, properties, durability and environmental benefits
author: Hamad, Ali Jihad
abstract: Concrete is the world's most used artificial material after water; however, using synthetic fibres for reinforcement brings about extensive environmental loads owing to their high energy requirements and large amounts of greenhouse gas emissions, in addition to non-biodegradability. It was these concerns, in addition to cost and performance limitations, which drove the switch to greener alternatives. Natural fibres (NFs), e.g., coir, jute, sisal, and hemp could be an alternative for eco-efficient construction solution which is naturally growable and biodegradable with low embodied energy. Natural fibres reinforced concrete (NFRC) has shown greater ductility, toughness, microcracking control and impact resistance in more concrete than with plain structural concrete used so that to give any particular shape to turn out concrete. The proposed methodology supports circular economy principles and contributes to reducing the environmental impact of construction materials through sustainable resource utilization. Nevertheless, the application of NFRC is more limited due to the fibre-incompatible matrix, since NF are hydrophilic and have low durability in an alkaline environment. This review is timely in that it collates previously disparate information on the mechanical, durability and environmental properties of NFRC which are of growing interest as sustainable construction materials. In addition to the positive effects and sustainable properties of using NFs in cementitious matrices (such as reducing greenhouse gases and less energy-consuming materials) the review findings add knowledge on how the fungal activity influences this interaction. We believe that what makes this paper novel is that it is a methodology paper that provides a global and holistic-view analysis of fresh, mechanical, durability, and environmental assessment delivering a common context that has not been suggested before. Furthermore, this review assesses optimization of fibre dosage, mechanisms of degradation, and limitations of the studies carried out to date relating engineering outputs to broader sustainability measures. Overall, this work effectively demonstrates a sound scientific basis towards the practical applications of nature-based optimized and nondestructive studied natural fibre reinforced composites on future sustainable concrete.

title: Polymer-regulated TiO_2/KCu^2+[Co^3+(CN)_6] nanocomposites with enhanced photochromism, color stability and tunable hue for durable rewritable paper
author: Wang, Jingwen
abstract: Prussian blue and its derivatives have attracted considerable attention in the field of rewritable paper due to their rich color changes and responsiveness to external stimuli. However, current Prussian blue-based rewritable paper are typically dependent on conductive materials, which limits their applicability in everyday scenarios; moreover, certain fabrication processes remain complex, hindering practical implementation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a polymer-regulated strategy by integrating TiO_2 nanoparticles and KCu^2+[Co^3+(CN)_6] particles with PVA or SA polymer coatings. The effects of polymer type and concentration on the hue, color density, and coloring time of the nanocomposite film are systematically investigated. PVA matrix achieves the longest color retention (up to 90 days), while SA matrix lasts 20 days, with polymer structure imparting black (PVA) or reddish-brown (SA) hues. The optimized rewritable paper exhibits excellent flexibility (tensile strength of 7.8 MPa, 40% elongation at break), which represents a marked enhancement compared to conventional adhesive-backed paper. Furthermore, it can be efficiently recolored by UV irradiation following 0.3% H_2O_2 vapor treatment, providing a controllable and practical strategy to advance the application of Prussian blue derivatives.

title: Engineering strategies, applications for safety and sustainability in chitosan-based emerging food systems
author: Ağgül, Ahmet Gökhan
abstract: Chitosan, a versatile and sustainable biopolymer, has emerged as a promising platform for developing advanced strategies in food safety and preservation. Its tunable molecular weight, degree of deacetylation, and hierarchical structure enable the rational design of diverse functional architectures, including nanostructures, coatings, membranes, and smart packaging systems with enhanced antimicrobial, antioxidant, barrier, and biocompatible properties. Beyond conventional preservation approaches, chitosan-based materials offer multifunctional solutions by extending shelf life, maintaining food quality, reducing environmental impacts, and enabling active and intelligent food packaging applications. Emerging applications include contaminant management strategies, such as microbial control and the adsorption of hazardous compounds, including aflatoxins and heavy metals. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the structural characteristics, modification strategies, functional properties, and diverse applications of chitosan-based materials in sustainable food protection systems. Furthermore, current challenges related to scalability, regulatory requirements, consumer acceptance, and commercialization are discussed, highlighting future perspectives for the successful translation of chitosan-based technologies into practical food applications. Graphical abstract

title: Cyclodextrin-cellulose composites: applications in food preservation, environmental remediation, and separation
author: Gu, Xuesong
abstract: In recent years, cyclodextrin-cellulose composite materials have attracted considerable interest due to the molecular recognition and encapsulation capabilities of cyclodextrin, as well as the structural integrity, sustainability and tunable surface chemical of cellulose. This review systematically outlines the structural characteristics of both components, summarizes key fabrication strategies, and analyzes their advance in multifaceted applications. Importantly, the performance of these composites originates not merely from the coexistence of the two building blocks, but from their synergistic effects: cellulose provides a robust, porous, and processable framework, while cyclodextrin contributes selective host-guest inclusion, interfacial recognition, and controlled-release capability. In food applications, these materials significantly enhance preservation and packaging performance by encapsulating antimicrobial and antioxidant agents; this enhancement is enabled by the synergy between the mechanical barrier function of cellulose matrices and the active-molecule hosting ability of cyclodextrin. In environmental remediation, they demonstrate outstanding adsorption and separation capabilities for water treatment, air purification, and the design of functional material. Furthermore, the unique cavity structure exhibits enantioselective separation for chiral drugs and sensing functions for detecting toxic alcohols. Finally, the review discusses the shortcomings of current research and looks forward to the future development trends of these materials in the directions of intelligent responsive materials.

title: Improved mechanical and thermal properties of PLA-based green nanocomposites through TPU, EVA, and PBAT blending
author: Vinodh, Sooraj
abstract: The present work examines the properties of polylactic acid (PLA) blended separately with thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), polyethylene vinyl acetate (EVA), and polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT) in a 70/30 weight ratio and compares them. The PLA blends were prepared using melt blending technique. Results indicate that significant differences were observed in the performance of these blends based on the minor portion of the polymer used. Furthermore, to alter the dispersion level and improve the blend properties, nanoclay was added at 3, 5, and 7 parts (parts per hundred resin), and their thermal and mechanical properties were analysed. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and the activation energy calculated based on kinetic studies show that all three individual blends without nanoclay have lower thermal stability than neat PLA. After the addition of nanoclay to the blend, the activation energy increased from 76 to 84.5 kJ/mol for PLA/TPU and from 83 to 92 kJ/mol for PLA/EVA at a nanoclay composition of 7 parts, compared with the neat blends. PLA/TPU based blends and nanocomposites show higher elongation, with 31% for neat blend and 79% and 87% at 3 and 5 parts nanoclay reinforcement, respectively. PLA/PBAT based biodegradable nanocomposites show moderate elongation of 30% and higher tensile strength of 32.5 MPa at 5 parts composition of nanoclay. In DSC cooling mode, a crystallization temperature peak of EVA at 70.4 °C and a peak of PBAT at 90.2 °C were observed. In FTIR analysis, only the PLA/TPU composition showed a change in peak position, indicating possible hydrogen bonding. Graphical abstract

title: Designing Polymer Electrolytes for Metal–Air Batteries: A Critical Review of Additive Strategies, Design Principles, and Future Directions
author: Adam, Abdullahi Abbas
journal: Journal of Inorganic and Organometallic Polymers and Materials
abstract: Metal–air batteries are promising energy-storage systems because of their high theoretical energy density, low-cost active materials, and potential suitability for flexible, wearable, and large-scale applications. However, their practical development remains limited by electrolyte leakage, insufficient ion transport, unstable electrode/electrolyte interfaces, metal-anode corrosion, dendrite formation, sluggish oxygen reactions, and poor long-term rechargeability. Polymer electrolytes offer a safer and more designable alternative to liquid electrolytes, but their performance depends strongly on the rational incorporation of functional additives. This review critically examines polymer electrolyte additives for metal–air batteries, focusing on how additive chemistry regulates ion transport, mechanical integrity, interfacial stability, metal deposition, corrosion suppression, and oxygen reduction/evolution reactions. The review further illustrates their mechanistic impact on interfacial phenomena at both the anode and cathode regions, comparing how additive-mediated interfacial kinetics differ across representative metal anodes. Unlike broader reviews on polymer electrolytes or general metal–air battery components, this work emphasises additive-centered design principles and additive-mediated mechanisms in polymer electrolyte-based systems. The review traces the evolution of additives from early plasticizers, salts, and inorganic fillers to multifunctional nanocomposites, ionic liquids, redox mediators, metal–organic frameworks, and bio-derived additives. Particular attention is given to additive effects at metal-anode and air–cathode interfaces across representative Zn-air, Li-air, Al-air, Na-air, Mg-air, and related systems, while distinguishing direct metal–air battery evidence from transferable mechanistic insights obtained from adjacent electrochemical systems. Recent progress in multi-additive formulations, wide-temperature operation, operando characterisation, modelling, machine-learning-assisted screening, safety, sustainability, and scale-up considerations is also discussed. Finally, the review identifies future directions for developing safe, scalable, and industrially relevant polymer electrolyte additives capable of enabling more durable and practical secondary metal–air batteries.

title: Effects of pre-vulcanisation on compounding, maturation, thermal stability, and mechanical properties of epoxidised natural rubber latex/citric acid/sulphur (ENR/CA/S) blend films
author: Abdul Ghani, Anis
abstract: This study explores the effect of using citric acid (CA) as a sustainable, non-toxic alternative green co-crosslinker in the preparation of pre-vulcanised ENR/CA/S blend films. The work also focuses on achieving complete pre-vulcanisation within 24 h by optimising both compounding time and maturation time. Results show that increasing the compounding time to 4 h reduces the toluene swell index (TSI) to 1.70. The incorporation of 5–10 phr of CA, in combination with sulphur, contributes to improved crosslinking characteristics, as reflected by a reduced TSI value and enhanced mechanical properties. However, pH remains the primary factor governing crosslink density, while CA plays a secondary role by promoting additional interactions within the network. The pH of the ENR/CA/S latex decreases as CA content increases. A low pH at high CA content significantly reduces both mechanical strength and thermal stability of ENR/15CA/S. The pre-vulcanised ENR/5CA/0.9S exhibits the optimal performance, with a tensile strength of 4.18 MPa and a glass transition temperature (T_g) of –21.77 °C. This work highlights the potential of CA as a vulcanising supportive crosslinker in a sulphur-based vulcanisation system for latex applications, which opens new possibilities for developing diverse latex-dipped products. Graphical abstract

title: Effect of temperature on dielectric behavior and charge transport mechanisms in PMMA/TBAI/Mg_1−xZn_xAl_2O_4 polymer nanocomposites
author: El-naggar, A. M.
journal: Journal of Materials Science: Materials in Electronics
abstract: PMMA/TBAI/Mg_1−xZn_xAl_2O_4, ( x = 0.0, 0.3, 0.5) nanocomposites were synthesized via solution casting. XRD and FTIR analyses confirmed filler integration and intermolecular interactions, while SEM revealed a rough morphology favoring interfacial polarization. All samples displayed high low-frequency dielectric constants ( ε ′) due to Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars polarization, with both ε ′ and ε ″ increasing with temperature. At 363 K and 1 kHz, the x = 0.0 composite exhibited the highest ε ′ (51.57) with low loss (0.97), while x = 0.3 showed higher loss (1.99). Relative energy density analysis ( E = 1 V/m) ranked pure PMMA highest (0.0251 J/m^3) due to negligible loss. AC conductivity followed Jonscher’s power law, peaking at 1.11 × 10⁻^7 S/cm for x = 0.3. Frequency exponent analysis revealed correlated barrier hopping for TBAI-containing samples, quantum mechanical tunneling for x = 0.0 and x = 0.5, and overlapping polaron behavior for PMMA. Impedance and modulus analyses confirmed thermally activated non-Debye relaxation with reduced bulk resistance at elevated temperatures. Zinc substitution effectively tailors dielectric and transport properties: x = 0.3 optimizes conductivity, while x = 0.0 and x = 0.5 provide high permittivity with low loss, making them promising candidates for advanced electronic applications.

title: A review of heating mechanisms, process parameters, and defect-minimized densification applications of microwave sintering in metals
author: Qiu, Qingyang
abstract: Microwave sintering, an advanced materials processing technique, has garnered substantial attention due to its distinctive heating mechanism, which facilitates more uniform and efficient heating of materials, such as metal powders. This study constructs a comprehensive analytical framework for metallic microwave sintering across diverse material systems, covering the trajectory from initial physical response to final microstructural evolution. By integrating fundamental electromagnetic loss mechanisms with multivariable coupled control logic, it offers essential theoretical support for the advancement of microwave metal processing. This paper emphasizes the fundamental principles of microwave-material interaction, incorporating key parameters like penetration depth and absorbed power. Furthermore, the impact of various factors on the sintering process, including metal powder particle size, sintering power, heating rates, sintering temperature, and sintering time was explored. The applications of microwave sintering across a range of materials in detail, such as ferroalloys, copper alloys, titanium alloys, tungsten alloys, silver, aluminum alloys, magnesium alloys, and high-entropy alloys (HEAs) were also presented. Microwave sintering imparts higher density and improved uniformity, thereby enhancing properties such as hardness, strength, and corrosion resistance. Lastly, this paper also addresses the challenges linked with the microwave sintering of metals and offers a comprehensive outlook. This research aims to provide valuable guidance and aid to scholars in this domain by delivering a detailed overview of the current state of microwave metal sintering.

title: Valorization of Glass Powder and Crushed Date Pits in Dune Sand Stabilization: A Geotechnical and Microstructural Approach
author: Zaidi, Lina
journal: Iranian Journal of Science and Technology, Transactions of Civil Engineering
abstract: Poor geotechnical properties of dune sand (DS) pose severe structural challenges in arid regions, while the accumulation of municipal and agricultural residues necessitates sustainable management strategies. This study evaluates the valorization of waste glass powder (GP) and organic crushed date pits (DP) as eco-friendly stabilizers to optimize the mechanical performance of dune sand DS. A comprehensive experimental campaign was conducted including standard Proctor compaction, direct shear, and California Bearing Ratio (CBR) tests. Standard Proctor, direct shear, and California Bearing Ratio (CBR) tests were conducted on DS blended with GP (2%, 4%, 6% and 8%) and DP (1%, 2%, 3% and 4%). Mechanical evaluations were coupled with microstructural analyses (XRF, XRD, SEM/EDX, TGA/DTG and FTIR) to elucidate the underlying stabilization mechanisms. Incorporating 6% GP maximizes technical performance, increasing the maximum dry density to 16.79 kN/m^3 for GP and to 16.30 kN/m^3 for DP (up from 16.12 kN/m^3 for untreated DS), generating an apparent cohesion of 32 kPa, and boosting the CBR index from 4.63 to 20.72%. Conversely, DP primarily enhances cohesion up to an optimal 3DP% (19 kPa), but reduces the internal friction angle (from 38.64° to 36.46° at 4 DP% and yields a limited CBR improvement (peaking at 8.48% for 1DP%) due to its lightweight, porous, and organic nature. Microstructural findings confirm a highly distributed filler effect and strong interparticle adhesion. These findings establish the synergistic valorization of industrial and agricultural wastes as a technically viable, low-carbon alternative to conventional binders in sustainable pavement engineering.

title: Advances in pacemaker powering: a review of energy harvesting mechanisms with emphasis on piezoelectric integration
author: Saxena, Shradha
abstract: The heart is an organ where continuity is essential. Therefore, the power supply required in a cardiac pacemaker must be designed very carefully. The study first presents an overview of the pacemaker, focusing mainly on lead configurations and programming approaches. On the basis of lead configuration, single chamber, dual chamber, and bi-ventricular pacemakers have been compared. Studies revealed that with dual chamber pacemakers, ~ 20–30% reduction in atrial fibrillation, ~ 80–90% reduction in pacemaker syndrome, and 10–15% increment in exercise tolerance, have been obtained than single chamber. In contrast, Bi-ventricular pacemakers show ~ 5–15% improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and ~ 41% improvement in heart failure patients. Similarly, a comparison of pacemakers has been carried out based on programming approaches, including fixed-rate, demand-based, and rate-adaptive. It is observed that rate-adaptive pacing offers superior physiological performance compared with fixed-rate and demand-based pacing, improving exercise capacity by ~ 25–45% and increasing maximum oxygen uptake by up to 41.5%. Next, self-sustaining energy harvesting techniques such as thermoelectric, electromagnetic, and piezoelectric have been studied and compared. It was found that the wide range of output power response (0.07 µW to 16 µW) has been attained with piezoelectric energy harvester (PEH). Furthermore, strategies for integrating PEHs with pacemakers have been compared, covering aspects such as design, material selection, implantation site and performance. It has been noted that, PMN-PT and PZT-based PEH with helical, buckled-beam, or fan-folded architectures demonstrate enhanced bio-compatibility with cardiac motion while enabling minimally invasive implantation within pacemakers or around pacing leads. Also, a brief discussion on the biocompatibility, durability, and long-term reliability of implantable self-powered pacemakers has been included. The review highlights that electrode materials such as platinum (Pt), platinum–iridium (Pt–Ir), gold (Au), titanium (Ti), along with lightweight and flexible device architectures, are essential for efficient energy harvesting, stable pacemaker operation, and long-term implantation.

title: Nanothermochromic smart windows: Nanostructures, doping and multifunctional strategies for high thermochromic performance
author: Ontiveros-Gómez, Luis Adrián
abstract: The rise of nanothermochromic materials for energy‑efficient glazing, recognizes windows as the major challenge for building energy losses and HVAC (Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning) demand as the sector that consumes more than 40% of total energy. The purpose of this paper is to provide a review following the PRISMA 2020 guided search on Scopus (2015–2026) to identify the most recent advances and remaining opportunities in thermochromic materials modified by nanotechnology. Vanadium dioxide (VO_2) has been established as an interesting material: across nanoparticles, patterned films, hybrid composites and nanoscale engineering that consistently improves luminous transmittance ( $${T}_{lum}$$ ), solar modulation ( $$\Delta {T}_{sol}$$ ) and tunes the phase transition temperature ( $${T}_{c}$$ ) toward room temperature while strengthening durability and manufacturability. Wet‑chemistry and physical routes yield size and phase‑controlled VO_2(M) compatible with scalable processing (inkjet, blade coating, sol–gel, hydrothermal synthesis, sputtering, atomic layer deposition). Elemental co‑doping lowers the Tc with manageable optical characteristics; multifunctional stacks integrate electro‑, photo‑ and mechano‑activation to accelerate switching and sharpen spectral selectivity; polymer matrices and hydrogels provide flexible, low‑cost routes to enhance $$\Delta {T}_{sol}$$ , and core–shell VO_2 architectures extend environmental stability. Nanothermochromic VO₂ have achieved advances such as high transmittance, strong solar modulation and lower transition temperatures through co‑doping, size control and scalable, durable designs, moving smart windows toward potential energy‑efficient application.

title: Sustainability of structural piles: New York City case studies and US application
author: Bhadiyadra, Vivek
abstract: The building industry accounts for 37–40% of total world-wide carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. Due to the large amount of embodied carbon in foundation systems this has brought attention to their use of energy. Structural Piles (Drilled Shafts, Augured Cast-In Place [ACIP] piles, Driven Steel HP Piles, Fiber Reinforced Polymer [FRP], Full Displacement Piles [FDP]) are a material intensive part of a structure that can also be an underutilized area when considering the entire structural carbon footprint. This study presents a synthesis of the literature concerning the environmental sustainability of pile foundations which were reviewed based on peer-reviewed articles between 2005 and 2025. In addition to the general studies on the sustainability of pile foundations; a number of these studies focused specifically on the environmental issues associated with New York City’s (NYC) subsoils and its implications to sustainable design. A second focus was made toward broadening the scope beyond NYC and examining the broader U.S. applicability. The literature presented in this study has been synthesized using verifiable data. Some key findings include: (1) The Global Warming Potential (GWP) due to steel production varies widely depending upon the method of production. EAF production generates GWP ranging from 0.36 to 0.70 t CO₂e/ tonne for scrap metal produced via electric arc furnaces to 2.0–2.3 t CO₂e/ tonne for BF-BOF production. Using a single reference set (BF-BOF 2.0–2.3 and scrap EAF 0.7 t CO₂e/tonne), the scrap-EAF route gives an approximately 65–70% lower GWP than the BF-BOF route; (2) Substitution of OPC with 50% GGBS results in a 41% reduction in GWP for concrete, whereas substituting OPC with 30% FA results in approximately a 21% reduction in GWP; (3) Optimization of pile geometry using computer modeling can result in reductions of 45–76% in embodied carbon compared to traditional industrial designs while maintaining identical specifications and code compliance; (4) Non-displacement cast-in-place techniques (CFA, ACIP and FDP) provide numerous benefits regarding construction phase sustainability including no spoils generated, significantly less noise and vibration and lower energy requirements during installation compared to impacts driven systems; and (5) Five major land mark NYC infrastructure projects Second Avenue Subway Phase I, LaGuardia Airport Terminal B, Hudson Yards Platform, One World Trade Center and the NYCHA Hurricane Sandy Recovery Program show how different approaches to geotechnical engineering and site specific engineering applications can respond to the documented subsurface variability of NYC’s soils. Verified sustainability attributes included LEED v4 Gold and Envision Platinum certification, optimized selection of materials through load test driven evaluation and innovative use of fiber reinforced concrete linings.

title: Quantifying environmental impacts and user experience in sustainable food packaging design
author: Zhang, Xiaonan
abstract: Sustainable food packaging design increasingly requires simultaneous consideration of environmental performance, food-protection function, and user experience, yet these dimensions are often quantified in separate literatures. This semi-systematic critical review synthesizes studies that assess environmental impacts through life cycle assessment (LCA) and studies that measure user experience (UX) through consumer, ergonomic, sensory, and behavioral evidence. The review is differentiated from conventional packaging-LCA reviews by focusing on the interfaces where LCIA method choice, system-boundary definition, food-waste modeling, disposal behavior, and usability evidence alter design conclusions. It first compares dominant LCIA frameworks, including CML, TRACI, ReCiPe, PEF, and related midpoint/endpoint approaches, showing why category-level transparency is essential for conventional, bio-based, compostable, and reusable packaging systems. It then maps UX dimensions such as opening convenience, safety perception, label comprehension, emptiability, aesthetics, and disposal accuracy to measurable methods, including force and torque testing, instrumental material characterization, sensory analysis, surveys, and observed behavior. Across the literature, environmental burden reduction often conflicts with consumer expectations: higher material intensity can reduce total system impacts when avoided food loss is included, while positive perceptions of biodegradable or compostable packaging can be offset by mis-sorting and infrastructure mismatch. The synthesis therefore argues for transparent, context-specific decision frameworks that connect LCA outputs, UX metrics, food waste evidence, and multi-criteria decision analysis rather than treating sustainability as a material label alone.

title: Single-use polypropylene cups manufacturing: lowering the environmental toll
author: Assali, Wael
journal: Journal of Material Cycles and Waste Management
abstract: Single-use plastic packaging is widely used, particularly in the food industry, and it causes significant environmental problems due to its low recycling rates and long environmental lifetime. This study investigates the environmental impact of polypropylene (PP) disposable plastic cups using life cycle analysis and real-world production data from a manufacturing plant. The system boundaries include the production and transportation of PP granules and packaging materials, as well as the cups’ manufacturing and packaging processes. Three improvement scenarios have been evaluated to reduce environmental impact: replacing PP with polylactic acid (PLA), incorporating renewable energy, and optimizing transportation routes. The results show that the largest environmental burdens come from the production and transport of PP granules, which has a significant impact on resources. Wind energy offers the most reliable reductions among renewable energy sources, and scenario analysis shows that switching to sea-based transportation routes can reduce environmental impacts by up to 45%. Furthermore, using PLA as an alternative raw material to PP significantly reduces toxicity and the use of fossil resources. However, the agricultural inputs required for PLA production contribute to increased eutrophication and acidification. These findings provide useful recommendations to legislators as well as those involved in the plastic sector. Graphical Abstract

title: Reinforcing the piezoelectric response of poly(vinylidene fluoride) based composites by using ZIF-8 hedgehog particles
author: Cui, Qingwen
journal: Journal of Materials Science: Materials in Electronics
abstract: Piezoelectric polymers represented by poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) have received increasing attention because of their great potential in realizing flexible piezoelectric sensors. However, one of the key obstacles that hinders the practical application of PVDF lies in the relatively low piezoelectric performance, i.e. piezoelectric coefficient d _33 (generally around 18–23 pC/N). Herein, we present a straightforward and effective strategy to enhance the piezoelectric response of PVDF by incorporating Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8 (ZIF-8) as reinforcing fillers. ZIF-8, with its unique hedgehog-like morphology and highly open framework structure, offers excellent compatibility with PVDF, facilitating strong interactions between the two components on a three-dimensional scale. Benefiting from the good interaction, enlarged piezoelectric phase content, strengthened interfacial coupling effect and consequently superior piezoelectric activities are realized in composites. For instance, upon an addition of 0.6 wt.% ZIF-8, a maximum piezoelectric coefficient d _33 of 34 pC/N can be obtained in the novel composites, which is 1.7 times that of pure PVDF film. Additionally, the feasibility and stability of composite in force-sensing is validated, highlighting its potential practical applications in piezoelectric sensors.

title: Modification of discarded PET molecular chains with methyl lactate endows the material with degradable properties
author: Wu, Ruzheng
abstract: The intrinsic stability and high crystallinity of discarded polyethylene terephthalate (dPET) make it highly resistant to natural degradation, posing a critical environmental challenge. Here, we report a facile phenolic esterification strategy using methyl lactate (DL) to convert dPET into a novel functional polymer (PBGs) that combines high mechanical strength with controlled degradability. The optimal dPET-to-DL ratio of 1:6 g·mL^− 1 yields the highest compressive strength, attributed to DL-induced chain extension and cross-linking. Structural analyses reveal that lactate incorporation disrupts chain regularity, increases amorphicity, and introduces hydrophilic hydroxyl groups, collectively facilitating water uptake and bulk degradation. Accelerated degradation tests show a three‑stage bulk erosion profile with mass losses of 0.22%, 4.12%, and 7.22% over 45 days, driven by chain scission, microcrack propagation, and oligomer plasticization. The modified material retains thermal stability while exhibiting much enhanced degradability relative to pristine dPET. This work offers a viable upcycling strategy to convert persistent dPET waste into a mechanically robust and environmentally degradable polymer, contributing to a sustainable plastic economy.

title: Revolutionizing Wearable Electronics: Zinc Oxide-Based Piezoelectric Nanogenerators for Mechanical Energy Harvesting
author: Korkmaz, S.
abstract: Piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) have attracted growing attention as self-powered devices that can convert low-frequency mechanical motions into electrical energy for wearable electronics, biomedical sensors, smart textiles, and portable microelectronic systems. Among various piezoelectric materials, zinc oxide (ZnO) is a particularly promising candidate because of its piezoelectric and semiconducting nature, wide bandgap, biocompatibility, low toxicity, low cost, and compatibility with flexible substrates. This review discusses the operating principles of ZnO-based PENGs and examines how crystal structure, morphology, doping, substrate selection, surface modification, and device architecture affect their output performance. Particular attention is given to ZnO nanowires, nanorods, nanosheets, nanoparticles, composite films, and hybrid structures produced by hydrothermal synthesis, chemical vapor deposition, electrochemical deposition, spin coating, and related fabrication methods. Recent progress in doped ZnO systems, polymer-supported structures, textile-integrated devices, and ZnO-based hybrid architectures is critically compared in terms of efficiency, flexibility, stability, cost, and practical applicability. The review also highlights current application trends in wearable electronics, biomedical devices, environmental monitoring, and self-powered sensing systems, while discussing remaining challenges such as low output power, charge screening, mechanical fatigue, humidity sensitivity, and large-scale fabrication. Finally, future perspectives are outlined, including artificial intelligence-assisted material design, conductive polymer/ZnO hybrids, bio-integrated systems, and fully integrated PENG platforms combining energy harvesting, storage, signal conversion, and sensing. This review provides a structured overview of ZnO-based PENGs and offers guidance for the design of next-generation flexible and self-powered energy-harvesting systems. Graphical Abstract

title: Thermal transport behaviour of glycerol-plasticised cassava starch/PVA composite films: A photoacoustic approach
author: Sreelakshmi, V S
abstract: The development of biodegradable, thermally insulating, and flexible substrates is essential for advancing sustainable wearable and flexible electronic technologies while reducing reliance on non-biodegradable synthetic polymers. In this work, cassava starch/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) composite films plasticised with glycerol are developed by solution casting and investigated for thermal diffusivity using photoacoustic spectroscopy. Glycerol content is varied from 0 wt% to 46.66 wt% to examine the influence of plasticisation on the functional and thermal transport behaviour of the films. The thermal diffusivity is found to decrease by 34.54%, indicating enhanced thermal insulation. Fourier transform infrared and Raman spectroscopic analyses confirm that glycerol incorporation introduces additional hydroxyl groups and weakens CH_2-CH_2 interactions within the polymer network. X-ray diffraction analysis confirms a gradual transition toward a more amorphous structure with increasing glycerol content. The thermal stability decreased from 225 °C for 0 wt% film to 167 °C for the 46.66 wt% plasticised film. Moisture absorption increases from 13.63% to 23.38%, whereas biodegradation improves from 40.04% to 80.64% from the unplasticised to plasticised films. When the tensile strength decreases from 3.985 MPa to 0.854 MPa, Young’s modulus also decreases from 1.074 MPa to 0.262 MPa, confirming enhanced flexibility of plasticised films. This work not only investigates the variation in thermal diffusivity upon glycerol plasticisation but also demonstrates the practical applicability of the optimised film with 9.30 wt% glycerol. The application of the optimised film in fabricating the substrate for a wearable temperature-monitoring device is also demonstrated, revealing its suitability for flexible electronics.

title: Deconstructing Microplastic Pollution in Terrestrial and Freshwater Environs: Holistic Assessment of Source Apportionment, Polymer-driven Ecological Hazard, and Human Exposure
author: Mohan, Kiruthika
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) in marine environments primarily originate from terrestrial sources, with 80% transported via river systems. This study analyzes the distribution, sources and ecological risks of MPs in the Krishnagiri District, Tamil Nadu, India. Source investigation through the Principal Component Analysis – Absolute Principal Component Scores – Multiple Linear Regression (PCA-APCS-MLR) model showed that single-use plastics and household waste contributed 60.3% of MPs in the terrestrial environment, followed by cosmetics, personal care products, and consumer goods at 23.4%, with durable long-term plastics contributing the least at 16.3%. The risk assessment indicated that the total pollution load is within Hazard level I in the Krishnagiri district. In particular, Aiyur, one of the primary seasonal Elephant corridors, exhibited a moderate to higher ecological risk, despite the lower MPs load. Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA) and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) analysis showed that there is no significant difference between each source class to explain the pollution load, and ecological risk indices. Group membership explained 14.7% of the variation in Potential Ecological Risk Index and 7.3% in Pollution Load Index, according to partial eta-squared values, highlighting that variability within the groups was more prominent. The average human consumption of MPs was higher through lake water (55 particles/year/kg) than through river water consumption (1 particle/year/kg). Higher pollutant load in lakes elevates the probability of human exposure, potentially resulting in more significant adverse health impacts. Therefore, it is imperative that risk assessment frameworks integrate measurements like Estimated Daily Index to more effectively identify potential consumption risks.

title: Enhancing the electrical conductivity of PEDOT:PSS with graphene quantum dots: a review of strategies, mechanisms, and device applications
author: Zhang, Yan
journal: Journal of Materials Science: Materials in Electronics
abstract: Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) is a widely used water-processable p-type conductive polymer with excellent transparency, environmental friendliness and flexibility. However, its intrinsic conductivity remains insufficient for next-generation flexible electronics and optoelectronic devices. Graphene quantum dots (GQDs), owing to their high conductivity, abundant specific surface area, and favorable aqueous dispersibility, have emerged as promising additives to enhance the electrical properties of PEDOT:PSS. This review systematically summarizes the synthesis approaches of GQDs, the doping strategies for GQDs/PEDOT:PSS composite films, the underlying mechanisms of conductivity enhancement, and recent applications in photovoltaics, sensors, and photodetectors. Emphasis is placed on the multiple synergistic effects of GQDs within PEDOT:PSS, including π–π interactions, conformational rearrangement of polymer chains, modulation of phase separation, and energy-level alignment, which can collectively facilitate charge transport.
