In addition, a comparative analysis of GQDs and other carbon-based nanomaterials (e.g., carbon quantum dots (CQDs), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), and graphene) is provided, highlighting dimensionality-dependent differences in conductivity-modulation mechanisms, dispersion behavior, interfacial compatibility, and surface tunability among carbon nanomaterials. Finally, key challenges and prospects are discussed.

title: Classification of defects in additive manufacturing processes according to their technologies, defect kinds, and underlying causes
author: Aniba, Sana
journal: International Journal on Interactive Design and Manufacturing (IJIDeM)
abstract: Industry 4.0 utilizes Additive Manufacturing (AM) due to its ability to offer flexibility and reduce waste; however, quality remains a significant obstacle: problems such as porosity, cracking, delamination, and dimensional defects limit its use in critical sectors. Nevertheless, no existing review offers a systematic classification of defects that encompasses all processes. This research addresses this gap by examining 165 academic works using the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) methodology, with support from an Artificial Intelligence tool (LLaMA3). The results indicate that defects fall into four categories: porosity and inclusions (45%), thermal issues (28%), layer adhesion problems (15%), and dimensional deviations (12%). The Ishikawa analysis of causes demonstrates that process (method) factors predominate in both metals (37%) and non-metals (31%), with a significant influence of the environment for metals (17%) and of the material itself for non-metals (26%). SLM (Selective Laser Melting) and FDM (Fused Deposition Modeling) technologies alone account for over 70% of the reported defects. This review goes beyond simple classification, it assesses the completeness of the reports in the corpus and identifies technology-specific challenges for defect reduction in the seven AM process categories. This work detects concrete opportunities to align machine learning research with industrial applications and offers practical recommendations, a technology selection guide, and future research priorities for the aerospace, medical, and manufacturing sectors in general. Graphical Abstract

title: A comprehensive review of advanced polymer coatings for corrosion protection: properties, applications, and innovations
author: Rzaij, Dina R.
journal: Journal of Coatings Technology and Research
abstract: Corrosion remains a considerable problem of concern in the chemical, petrochemical, marine, and energy industries as it is detrimental to the integrity, safety in operation, and costs of maintenance of the equipment. Advanced polymer coatings have emerged as promising candidates based on their tunable chemical properties, high barrier resistance, and compatibility with different functional additives. This review critically examines progress made in polymer-based corrosion protection technologies since 2015 through 2025. It emphasizes their fundamental mechanisms, essential performance properties, and recent advancements. Notably, literature shows significant quantitative improvements such as one to three orders of magnitude enhancement of impedance modulus, inhibition efficiencies over 90%, and extended salt-spray resistance up to 1200 h for best optimized nanocomposite systems. In this work, we will discuss recent development trends including nanostructured coatings, self-healing polymers based on intelligent frameworks, graphene composites, and eco-friendly inhibitors. This review integrates information based on spectroscopy and electrochemical studies. The review also identifies current issues including agglomeration of nanofillers, concerns regarding long-term durability, and difficulties associated with large-scale manufacturing. Finally, future aspects for research are suggested that explore multifunctional hybrid materials, stimuli-responsive coating schemes, sustainable inhibitor systems, or strategies for industrial process scale-up. This is a reference that could be well utilized by researchers and engineers to formulate more durable, sustainable, and high-performance corrosion protection solutions.

title: Preparation and anti-corrosion performance of CKPU-NE composite coatings
author: Qiu, Yuzhe
abstract: To meet the requirements for metal protection in harsh environments, this study aims to develop a vegetable oil-based polyurethane coating system that combines high hydrophobicity with long-lasting corrosion resistance. First, Castor oil-based polyurethane (CO-PU) was synthesised, which was then modified using the silane coupling agent KH-560 to produce CKPU. Nano-SiO_2 was introduced via in situ polymerisation, and the doping level was optimised to produce the nano-composite coating CKPU-Nano. Furthermore, three types of epoxy resins (E44, E51 and E54) were grafted to form the CKPU-NE series of composites. Scanning electron microscopy(SEM) was employed to examine microstructural dispersion, whilst physical, hydrophobic and anti-corrosion properties were systematically tested. These were supplemented by electrochemical (EIS, polarisation), long-term immersion and salt spray tests for a comprehensive evaluation. The results indicate that the CKPU-NE coating containing 3 wt% of epoxy resin E54 exhibits the best overall performance: the water contact angle increased from 93° in the base coating to 98.5°, and the water absorption rate was as low as 8.10%. The corrosion current density was only 6.45 × 10^− 8 A/cm^2, and the polarisation resistance reached 2338.9 kΩ·cm^2. Long-term tests showed that the degree of surface corrosion was significantly less severe than that of the control samples, confirming that this coating possesses excellent long-term protective capabilities. Graphical abstract

title: Mechanisms of water-inrush mitigation under alternative grouting strategies during shaft sinking: Solidification-enabled stress–seepage–damage coupling
author: Li, Wenxin
journal: Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment
abstract: Vertical shaft excavation in faulted ground is prone to establishing hydraulic connection with adjacent aquifers, thereby triggering water inrush. Although grouting is commonly employed as a mitigation measure, the mechanisms responsible for performance variations among different grouting schemes remain insufficiently understood. In this study, grout diffusion–deposition and hydration-driven solidification are integrated into a coupled stress–seepage–damage framework. A full-process model encompassing grouting, solidification, and excavation-induced disturbance is developed and validated through laboratory experiments. Within an “aquifer–fault–shaft” configuration, a unified indicator system is established to benchmark surrounding rock grouting, fault grouting, and aquifer grouting, thereby delineating their mechanistic differences. Results show that all schemes reduce the seepage velocity at the shaft boundary by more than 90%, yet they operate through distinct controlling pathways. Aquifer grouting provides the most effective water blocking, primarily by weakening the water source supply. Fault grouting achieves the most pronounced reinforcement and hydraulic disconnection by transforming the dominant water-conducting channels. Surrounding rock grouting enhances near-field stability, strengthens resistance to excavation-induced disturbance, and postpones channel coalescence and breakthrough. Collectively, the proposed “source weakening–channel blocking–disturbance regulation” mechanistic interpretation provides a basis for dominant-factor-oriented strategy selection and optimization.

title: Accelerating the development of protein-based materials: Automation as a tool for materials advancement
author: Komatsu, Yasuhiko
abstract: The design-build-test-analyze (DBTA) cycle is a powerful framework for accelerating discovery across macromolecular materials; moreover, recent advances in synthesis, characterization, and computational modeling have increased the feasibility of integrated, iterative workflows. Protein-based materials are a compelling target for a DBTA workflow, as their monomer-level sequence control facilitates precise structure–property studies, and their vast design space and diverse use cases require new high-throughput and automated methods. In this Prospective, we highlight opportunities in each stage of the protein-materials DBTA cycle in which automated and data-driven approaches can alleviate current bottlenecks and drive efficient discovery of high-performance materials. Graphical abstract

title: Exploring new approaches to enhance polyhydroxybutyrate accumulation in Paracoccus denitrificans
author: Fukala, Ivo
journal: World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology
abstract: The bacterium Paracoccus denitrificans was investigated for polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) production on eight organic carbon substrates. Aerobic cultivation on crotonate resulted in the most significant PHB accumulation. Additionally, PHB production on butyrate increased with an addition of HCO₃⁻ to the mineral medium. Based on the substrate specificity of the cell fraction and the results of the reverse transcription quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for the related gene, it is likely that butyrate and crotonate activations are catalyzed by propionyl-CoA synthetase. Potential FnrP-like binding sequences were identified upstream of certain genes related to PHB metabolism, and RT-qPCR confirmed different expression levels of the concerned genes. FnrP mutant exhibits higher PHB accumulation than the wild-type when grown anaerobically on butyrate and crotonate, transmission electron microscopy revealed an accumulation of PHB granules in the FnrP^− strain. Membrane inlet mass spectrometry demonstrated that the FnrP mutant has an impaired denitrification pathway. The Paracoccus denitrificans citrate synthase was shown to be allosterically regulated by the NAD^+/NADH ratio and activated by Na^+, K^+, and NH_4^+ ions. K^+ limitation during aerobic growth led to increased PHB accumulation.

title: Development of Single and Hybrid AA6063 Metal Matrix Composites Reinforced with Metallurgical Slag Powders
author: Amra, Rana H.
abstract: Al-ceramic particulate metal matrix composites are promising materials for structural and advanced engineering applications because of their enhanced mechanical properties and low weight. However, metallurgical slags, including electric arc furnace (EAF), ladle refining furnace (LRF), copper (Cu), manganese (Mn), and aluminum (Al) slags, are generated as industrial by-products and represent a source of environmental contamination. In this study, the feasibility of using these metallurgical slags as reinforcement materials in an AA6063 matrix was investigated. The composites were fabricated as single and hybrid systems using stir casting followed by cumulative hot rolling. The mechanical performance was interpreted based on several strengthening mechanisms, including Orowan strengthening from finely dispersed phases, load transfer due to improved interfacial bonding, grain refinement induced by hot rolling, and dislocation strengthening caused by thermal expansion mismatch between the matrix and reinforcement. The results showed that hybrid composites containing Al and LRF slags exhibited improved properties due to the presence of spinel (MgAl_2O_4) and silica (SiO_2) phases, which enhanced interfacial integrity and acted as barriers to dislocation motion. In addition, hot rolling significantly improved the mechanical properties of the developed composites. Among all compositions, the LRF/Cu hybrid slag composite exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a hardness of 125 HV, an ultimate tensile strength of 223 MPa, elongation of 9.8%, and weight loss of 1%. These findings confirm that metallurgical slags, particularly in hybrid form, can effectively enhance multiple properties of AA6063 composites and provide a promising approach for developing sustainable and high-performance aluminum matrix composites. Graphical Abstract  Hybrid metallurgical slags successfully reinforced AA6063 matrix composites through stir casting and hot rolling. Hybrid slag systems improved hardness, tensile strength, and wear resistance through synergistic strengthening mechanisms. Hot rolling enhanced densification, reduced porosity, and promoted more uniform particle redistribution within the matrix. MgAl_2O_4 and SiO_2-related phases improved interfacial integrity and contributed to effective load transfer behavior.

title: Radiation shielding and optical properties of phosphate glass doped with Yb_2O_3 and Er_2O_3
author: Agha, Ahmad Rabie
abstract: In this study a new glass system of 47P_2O_5 – 24PbO – 6Al_2O_3 – [23-(x + y)] Na_2O- (x)Er_2O_3- (y)Yb_2O_3 (x = 0, and 0.5; y = 0, 0.5, and 1 mol%) was prepared. In addition to the pristine sample (x = 0, y = 0 mol%), 0.5 mol% of Na_2O was replaced with Yb_2O_3 (x = 0, y = 0.5 mol%) in the second sample, and with Er_2O_3 (x = 0.5, y = 0 mol%) in the third one. In the fourth sample, 1.5 mol% of Na_2O was replaced with a combination of 1% Yb_2O_3 and 0.5% Er_2O_3 (x = 0.5, y = 1 mol%). The addition of 0.5 mol% Yb_2O_3 yielded the highest optical basicity (Λ), attributed to an increase in the negative charge on the oxygen atoms, and an enhancement of the covalency in the cation-oxygen bonding. The third-order nonlinear susceptibility (χ^(3)) of the studied glasses was enhanced by adding Yb_2O_3, Er_2O_3, or their mixture, suggesting their potential for optoelectronic applications. To verify the ability of using the studied glass for radiation shielding, the values of the mass attenuation coefficient (µ_m), linear attenuation coefficient (LAC), half-value layer (HVL), mean free path (MFP), tenth-value layer (TVL), and effective atomic number (Z_eff) were calculated using both the Monte Carlo simulation code and the Phy-X/PSD program software. The results showed a noticeable increase in LAC values for samples containing Yb_2O_3 or Er_2O_3, improving the radiation protection properties of glass, with the best results obtained with Yb_2O_3/Er_2O_3-containing glass.

title: Carbazole-based aqueous supramolecular organic frameworks enabling cascade energy transfer-regulated ROS photocatalysis for metal-free C–S and P–S bond formation
author: Liu, Jian-Yue
abstract: 构筑兼具高效多步能量传递和多功能光催化活性的水相超分子有机框架仍然是人工光合作用的核心挑战. 本文通过葫芦[8]脲介导的主客体识别组装了一种基于咔唑的二维超分子有机框架, 随后依次引入罗丹明B (RhB)和Cy5, 实现了在水中的连续荧光共振能量传递(FRET), 第二步效率高达91.4%. 连续能量传递调控活性氧的生成, 增强了超氧阴离子自由基(O_2^•−)的产生, 使得在温和的水相条件下, 无需金属催化剂即可实现广谱底物适用的需氧C–S和P–S键形成. 机理研究揭示了O_2^•−介导的硫自由基途径, 该途径直接耦合了超分子能量转移和选择性成键. 这项工作为多功能水相超分子光催化剂的设计奠定了基础, 并推动了基于超分子有机框架的可持续光化学合成的发展. Constructing aqueous supramolecular organic frameworks (SOFs) that integrate efficient multistep energy transfer with versatile photocatalytic reactivity remains a central challenge in artificial photosynthesis. Herein, a carbazole-based two-dimensional SOF is assembled via cucurbit [8]uril-mediated host-guest recognition, followed by sequential incorporation of Rhodamine B (RhB) and Sulfo-Cyanine5 (Cy5) to enable cascade fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) with a second-step efficiency of 91.4% in water. The cascade energy migration regulates reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation toward enhanced superoxide anion radicals (O_2^•−) production, allowing metal-free aerobic C–S and P–S bond formation under mild aqueous conditions with broad substrate scope. Mechanistic studies reveal an O_2^•−-mediated sulfur radical pathway that directly couples supramolecular energy transfer with selective bond construction. This work establishes design principles for multifunctional aqueous supramolecular photocatalysts and advances sustainable photochemical synthesis based on SOFs.

title: Adaptive neuro-fuzzy capsule network optimised by Salp Swarm Algorithm for simultaneous prediction of strength and durability indices in sustainable PET–RHA concrete
author: Kumar, Pololy Pradeep
abstract: Concrete is a sustainable alternative to conventional concrete, which incorporates recycled polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and rice husk ash (RHA). Also, the complexity of nonlinear interactions between all mix constituents makes accurately predicting their mechanical and durability properties difficult. In addition, knowledge in engineering is mainly expressed in qualitative form and not in a strictly numerical relation. So, conventional regression techniques or standard deep learning models may not work effectively. The objective of the research is to put forth an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Capsule Network optimised by Salp Swarm Algorithm (ANFCapsNet-SSA) capable of predicting and assessing simultaneously the compressive strength (CS), splitting tensile strength (STS), flexural strength (FS), water absorption (WA), modulus of elasticity (MoE) and rapid chloride permeability (RCPT) of concrete. A merged framework proposed which the ANFIS (Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference system) and capsule network (CapsNet) to capture fuzzy linguistic knowledge of expert and a complex non-linear relationship within the experimental dataset. The ANFIS module converts the input that are typically mix-design variables into fuzzy feature forms that is intePretable, while the CapsNet learns hierarchical statistical patterns on the input via dynamic routing by agreement. The learned relationships, which are inherently data-driven and designed for predictive modelling, do not explicitly represent the underlying physics or chemistry of concrete behaviour. For improved model performance, Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) will optimise the hyper parameters of integrated ANFIS-CapsNet architecture. The Conditional Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (CGAN-GP) generates statistically consistent synthetic training samples to mitigate the limitation of the experimental dataset while Gradient-weighted Relevance Propagation (GRP) supplies post hoc interpretation of the contribution of each input variable to predicted outputs. The analysis of the suggested scheme is based on a 90-day experimental dataset. Of all the models that were investigated, the ANFCapsNet-SSA showed the best predictive performance with R² = 0.9993, MAE = 0.0007, RMSE = 0.0019, MAPE = 0.006%, EVS = 0.9941, RSR = 0.000171, CPI = 0.9968. The proposed framework can thus be quite useful as a decision-support tool in designing and evaluating the performance of sustainable PET-RHA concrete as evidenced by the strong predictive power of the framework for the considered dataset.

title: Hyperbranched Polyester/Rubber Powder Improves Epoxy Asphalt Mechanical and Aging Performance
author: Zou, Xiaolong
journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
abstract: To address the performance degradation of epoxy asphalt under UV radiation and oxygen, laboratory-simulated UV-accelerated aging tests were conducted. The mechanical properties, microstructure, and chemical structure of hyperbranched polyester/rubber powder composite-toughened epoxy asphalt were investigated. Tensile test results indicate that with increasing aging time, fracture elongation and tensile strength decrease. The sample with 3%H-10%R showed the smallest reductions, demonstrating optimal aging resistance. Fluorescence and scanning electron microscopy revealed that hyperbranched polyester inhibits oxidative degradation by forming a three-dimensional crosslinked network, while rubber powder delays asphalt deterioration through UV absorption and radical scavenging. Their combined action improved system compatibility. FTIR spectroscopy showed that the composite effectively mitigated the increase in carbonyl index; after 6 days of aging, the carbonyl index decreased by 26% compared with unmodified epoxy asphalt. The combined toughening system exerts an anti-aging effect by scavenging free radicals and blocking oxidation pathways. This study provides a feasible modification scheme for high‑durability epoxy asphalt used in bridge deck pavement.

title: Employing Density Separation to Characterise Microplastic Contamination in Coastal Wetland Ecosystems
author: Cousins, Abigail
abstract: The study investigates microplastic (MP) contamination across three coastal wetland ecosystems: seagrass, saltmarsh, and mangroves. The study aimed to employ a density separation technique to characterise the extent and composition of MP contamination, providing a comprehensive analysis of the trends in distribution and morphology. Despite the growing body of research on MPs, there remains a lack of detailed, localised studies focusing on coastal wetland ecosystems, which may be effective sinks for MP pollution, acting as a Nature-based Solution. Seagrass meadows exhibited a predominant input of MPs from marine sources, with fibres accounting for 60.5% of the total MP content. Saltmarsh sediments showed a similar dominance of fibres (62.3%), linked to wastewater inputs. Mangroves, however, displayed the highest MP concentration, dominated by fragments (59.7%), likely due to the fragmentation of larger plastic debris deposited during storm surges. MP colour patterns were also ecosystem-specific, with red MPs being prevalent in seagrass (55.0%) and saltmarsh (39.9%) and transparent being most prevalent in mangroves (73.4%). The study emphasises the ecological implications of MP contamination, including risks to marine species and the potential disruption of sediment biogeochemistry, warranting further investigation into the long-term effects on coastal ecosystems. Graphical Abstract  Seagrass beds trap MPs primarily from marine sources, with fibres potentially dominating due to synthetic rope degradation and wastewater inputs. Saltmarshes retain MPs differently based on plant species, with Salicornia marshes showing the highest MP concentration. Mangroves exhibit the highest MP concentration, particularly near shorelines, with fragments being common potentially due to storm-driven debris and boat traffic.

title: Quantitative evaluation of coloration and functionalization efficiency for surface modification of regenerated cellulose fabrics
author: Gaafer, Rania Rashad Tawakol
abstract: Globally, the ever-growing demand for sustainable, functionalized cellulosic textile fabrics has increased, steering interest towards a new generation of eco-friendly regenerated cellulosic fibers. In this study, sustainable dyed and multi-functionalized Tencel and bamboo fabrics were developed via eco-friendly surface modification, followed by dyeing with natural dyes in the presence or absence of essential oils to fabricate multi-functionalized cellulosic dyeings in a single step. First, Tencel and Bamboo fabrics were modified using biopolymers, namely gelatin (10 g/L) /β-cyclodextrin (7 g/L) in the presence of citric acid/sodium hypophosphite as an environmentally benign crosslinking system via a pad–dry–cure technique. Subsequently, the pre-modified fabrics were dyed with turmeric dye or Natural Brown 6 dye with or without essential oils, namely clove, cinnamon, and tulsi (20 g/L). FT-IR analysis, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, along with quantitative and qualitative evaluations, were performed. The results obtained revealed a significant improvement in antibacterial activity with bacterial reduction percentages exceeding 90%. In addition, excellent ultraviolet protection properties were achieved. The integration of natural dyes and essential oils within the biopolymers resulted in durable coloration, improved functionality, and enhanced performance properties while maintaining air permeability within a reasonable range. The developed approach represents an environmentally benign and effective strategy for producing added-value sustainable textiles with combined aesthetic and protective functionality.

title: Animal degradation of microbial storage polyhydroxyalkanoates
author: Zeidler, Caroline
abstract: This study shows that the degradation of microbial storage polyhydroxyalkanoates is not just restricted to microorganisms by finding that some animals also have the enzymes required to break down these biopolymers. A wide range of microorganisms produce storage biopolymer polyhydroxyalkanoates (sPHAs) as carbon and energy reserves. However, only bacteria and fungi are known to degrade microbial sPHAs, using enzymes called polyhydroxyalkanoate depolymerases (PHADs). Here we show that some animals also have PHADs that can degrade sPHAs. We discovered a PHAD in the gutless oligochaete Olavius algarvensis , a marine worm that gains nutrition by digesting bacterial symbionts, including a dominant symbiont in which sPHAs account for up to 42% of cellular carbon stores. Enzyme assays, combined with mass spectrometry, confirmed that heterologously expressed O. algarvensis PHAD degraded sPHAs into hydroxyalkanoate monomers that can enter conserved metabolic pathways. Imaging of mRNA showed that PHAD was expressed in the oligochaete epidermis, the site of symbiont digestion. We further identified PHADs in more than 66 gut-bearing animal species from nine phyla and 19 protist species from three major supergroups, suggesting that the last common ancestor of metazoans possessed PHADs. Functional assays confirmed that PHADs from phylogenetically distant animal lineages spanning aquatic and terrestrial environments degrade sPHAs. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized pathway by which protists and animals can access microbial carbon reserves, with broad relevance given the widespread occurrence of sPHAs across ecosystems.

title: Polar-Twisted Electron-Transport Layer Simultaneously Breaks Efficiency-Flexibility-Cost Limits in Organic Solar Cells
author: Huyen Mai, Thi
abstract: A polar-twisted perylene diimide electron-transport layers framework enables additive-free alcohol processing, suppressed over-crystallization, and improved oxidative stability. H75-DMA delivers over 20% efficiency in binary organic solar cells while retaining ~ 80% of its initial power conversion efficiency after 384 h air storage. H75-DMA enhances flexible and semitransparent organic solar cells and enables Ag-to-Cu cathode substitution with 18.65% efficiency, highlighting device-level cost effectiveness while approaching Ag-based performance. Perylene diimide (PDI)-based electron-transport layers (ETLs) are fundamental in governing charge extraction, interfacial recombination, and the operational longevity of organic solar cells (OSCs), yet their molecular design still lacks transferable principles. Here we present a PDI-ETL molecular design framework that couples bay-position engineering with polar, bulky side-chain modulation to improve additive-free alcohol solubility, suppress over-crystallization, and mitigate oxidative degradation. With this framework, H75-DMA suppresses reactive-oxygen-driven chemical evolution and interfacial trap accumulation, thereby stabilizing interfacial energetics and electron transport. Binary OSCs based on H75-DMA achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) above 20% and exhibit improved mechanical toughness and bending durability in flexible devices. Its smooth, high-surface-energy interface also induces continuous growth of ultrathin metal cathodes, leading to increased light-utilization efficiency in flexible semitransparent OSCs. In addition, H75-DMA enables cathode substitution from Ag to Cu while retaining about 97% of the PCE of the Ag-based devices, thereby improving cost-effectiveness at the device level.

title: Sustainable compounding: innovations in green ingredients for the rubber industry
author: Musa, Muhamad Sharan
abstract: The rubber industry is under increasing pressure to reduce its environmental footprint while maintaining high material performance and industrial scalability. This review examines recent advances in sustainable rubber compounding, focusing on green ingredients such as bio-based fillers, recycled carbon black, renewable plasticisers, and environmentally benign vulcanisation systems. Particular emphasis is placed on structure–property relationships, highlighting how bio-derived functional groups influence filler–rubber interactions, crosslinking behaviour, and viscoelastic performance. Recent studies demonstrate that partial substitution of conventional petroleum-based additives with sustainable alternatives can achieve comparable mechanical performance, improved ageing resistance, and reduced environmental impact when formulation strategies are carefully optimised. Industrial case studies further demonstrate the growing commercial viability of these materials. Key challenges remain in achieving consistent material quality, ensuring compatibility with existing processing technologies, and balancing performance trade-offs. This review provides a formulation-oriented perspective and outlines future directions toward scalable, high-performance, and environmentally responsible rubber materials.

title: Biological and synthetic biology strategies for polystyrene degradation: mechanisms, microbial advances, and circular economy perspectives
author: Nazir, Mehar
abstract: Polystyrene (PS), a petroleum-based synthetic polymer which is extensively used in packaging, insulation, and consumer goods, has emerged as a major environmental pollutant. This report provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in biological and synthetic biology strategies for novel PS-degrading microorganisms, including bacteria and fungi isolated from unique ecosystems such as insect gut microbiomes and extreme environments. Insects like mealworms and superworms have demonstrated the ability to ingest and degrade PS through symbiotic microbial activity, while fungi such as Aspergillus tubingensis and marine-derived fungi contribute enzymatically to polymer breakdown. Advances in enzymology involving oxidative enzymes like laccases and peroxidases have improved our understanding of PS degradation at the molecular level, supported by innovations in enzyme engineering and immobilization. The paper also examines the biodegradation abilities of bacteria, fungi, and microbes associated with insects and critically analyzes the methods used for degradation assessments, differentiating between genuine biodegradation and mineralization versus surface oxidation, fragmentation, and reduction in polymer weight. Moreover, the advancements in synthetic biology, which include metabolic engineering and engineered microbial consortia, and the biological upcycling of PS intermediates to valuable products, are also covered in light of the circular economy approach. title: Hyemo as Emotional Politics in Digital Feminism: The Case of the 4B Movement in South Korea
author: Shin-Winans, Daeun
abstract: This study examines the role of hyemo–a Korean emotion category–in shaping the discourse of the 4B movement in South Korea, a digital feminist initiative that rejects heteronormative practices, such as childbirth, dating, marriage, and sexual intercourse. Drawing on Nussbaum’s socio-cognitive approach to emotion and Foucault’s concept of neoliberal governmentality, the study employs social actor analysis of the online community, Yeosungsidae ‘Women’s Generation.’ The analysis reveals that hyemo encodes relational patterns of other-blaming and other-inferiorizing directed at Korean men and Korean women in heterosexual relationships. In the construction of these patterns, the neoliberal imperative of self-optimization serves as the barometer for morality and social superiority. By framing heterosexuality as a site for the contamination of inferiority and moral failure, the movement positions the rejection of heterosexual activity as a form of avoidance and retaliation. Ultimately, the study argues that hyemo–by encoding a set of patterns of relationship constructed through the logic of contamination–explains the intersection of seemingly conflicting characteristics within the 4B movement, namely feminist resistance against patriarchy and the emergence of exclusionary identity politics.

title: Underwater-Adhesive, Stretchable Fabric Dry Electrode Based on a Novel Graphene Oxide Aqueous Polyurethane for Electrophysiological Monitoring
author: Li, Rui
abstract: Electronic textiles (E-textiles) provide remarkable potential for next-generation personalized healthcare. However, the limitations in skin adhesion, underwater stability, and air permeability severely hinder their broader application, especially in dynamic and aquatic environments during sweating, showering, or underwater conditions. Here, we reported a highly skin-adhesive, underwater-stable, and breathable E-textile enabled by a graphene oxide–aqueous polyurethane (GAWPU) intermolecular network integrated with a macroscopic knitting structure. Mechanical testing on porcine skin demonstrates an exceptional shear adhesion strength (665 kPa), outperforming previously reported E-textile self-adhesive materials. Benefiting from its multi-scale architecture design, the knitted E-textile also exhibits high stretchability (> 300%) together with breathable waterproofness (466 ± 5 mm/s). The intrinsic water resistance and strong adhesiveness of the GAWPU network allow the E-textile to adhere firmly to biological tissues in wet environments, even for under-water scenarios. As a proof of concept, the E-textile is successfully used as a water-resistant electrode sensor for monitoring diverse human electrophysiological signals, such as surface electromyography (sEMG) and electrocardiography (ECG). Moreover, GAWPU's extraordinary biocompatibility and antibacterial properties enable prolonged skin contact without irritation. This E-textile forms a unified platform integrating tissue adhesion, environmental stability, and biosensing, paving the way for deploying textile-based electronics in real-world biomedical and interactive applications.

title: Thermal Protective Performance of Firefighter Clothing: A Review of Advances in Heat, Moisture, Materials, and Physiological Safety
author: Kumar, Virendra
abstract: Firefighters routinely operate in extreme thermal environments where exposure to radiant heat, flames, and flash fires can degrade the protective performance of firefighter protective clothing. The effectiveness of these garments depends on key properties such as thermal insulation, reflectivity, porosity, and moisture management. While thermal insulation limits heat transfer to the skin, moisture accumulation from perspiration or environmental humidity can enhance heat and mass transfer within the clothing system. Moisture evaporation and condensation further exacerbate thermal stress, increasing the likelihood of burn injuries. This review critically examines the thermal protective performance of firefighter garments under high-temperature and moisture-rich conditions. It synthesizes current knowledge on coupled heat and moisture transport, fabric architecture, air-gap effects, material properties, and multilayer garment configurations. Advances in experimental characterization, numerical modeling, and predictive assessment of thermal degradation are also evaluated. Finally, key research gaps and future directions are highlighted to improve garment aging assessment, damage quantification, and service-life prediction, thereby supporting the development of safer, more durable, and high-performance firefighter protective systems.

title: Modified starches for fluid loss control in water-based drilling fluids: A systematic review and future perspectives for sago-based approaches
author: Pramana, Yanuar Sigit
abstract: Starch remains one of the most practical and sustainable biopolymers for fluid-loss control in water-based drilling fluids (WBDFs), yet its native thermal and ionic limitations restrict performance under demanding downhole conditions. This systematic review synthesizes advances in starch-based fluid-loss reducers by screening eligible studies published between 2010 and 2025 and examining how physical, chemical, and hybrid modification strategies influence hydration behavior, thermal stability, filtration control, and rheological performance in WBDF systems under saline and elevated-temperature conditions. Physical treatments such as gelatinization, pregelatinization, micronization, and nanogrinding primarily improve hydration, granule disintegration, pore plugging, and interparticle bridging, but their performance window is often narrower than that of chemically modified or hybrid-modified systems. The thermomechanical characteristics of sago starch suggest that it may be a promising candidate for extrusion-based pregelatinization aimed at achieving cold-water solubility without excessive loss of thermal integrity. Chemical modification generally provides more durable performance under elevated temperature and salinity. Crosslinked and graft-copolymerized starches more often outperform simple etherified derivatives, while carboxymethylated starch offers improved hydration capacity and saline compatibility, making it an effective component in more integrated designs. Among the reviewed routes, hybrid-modified starches, which combine ionic, hydrophobic, or network-forming functionalities, provide the most balanced improvements in thermal endurance, ionic tolerance, and overall WBDF performance. Despite these advances, the literature remains fragmented by inconsistent testing practices and limited technoeconomic or environmental assessment. This review consolidates the current evidence, identifies critical research gaps, and highlights the underexplored potential of sago starch as a feedstock for next-generation WBDF fluid-loss reducers.

title: Coinage-Metal-Based Nanostructures: Multifunctional Nanomaterials for Energy Harvesting
author: Che Lah, Nurul Akmal
abstract: Internet of Nano-Things (IoNT) drives the need for autonomous energy solutions that can operate under low‑grade, high‑entropy ambient conditions. This review examines coinage metal nanostructures—namely, Au, Ag, and Cu—as multifunctional materials for next‑generation energy‑harvesting platforms. Beyond elemental systems, selected coinage‑metal‑containing compounds are included where they play a direct mechanistic role in energy conversion. These nanostructures exhibit tunable electronic properties, high surface reactivity, and strong coupling phenomena, enabling their integration into diverse transduction mechanisms, including flexoelectric, plasmonic, piezoelectric, thermoelectric, magnetostrictive, and triboelectric systems. Strategies for performance optimization, such as surface functionalization, morphological control, and composite formation, are discussed in relation to interfacial interactions, charge transport, and structural stability. Sustainability considerations, including material availability, recyclability, and scalability, are also addressed. By synthesizing recent advances across material science, nanotechnology, and energy engineering, this review provides a forward‑looking perspective on the design of coinage-metal‑based nanogenerators for self‑powered systems in distributed IoNT environments.

title: Effects of mechanical treatment, salt, and temperature on the properties of lignin-containing cellulose nanofibril/bentonite drilling fluids
author: Noor, Abdullahi Ahmed
abstract: Lignin-containing cellulose nanofibrils (L-CNFs) are promising rheological and filtration modifiers for bentonite water-based drilling fluids (BT-WBDFs); however, their tendency to aggregate severely limits their effectiveness. This study investigates the effects of further mechanical treatment, salt concentration, and temperature on the rheological and filtration properties of L-CNF/BT-WBDFs. Further mechanical treatment, including wet grinding and high-pressure homogenization, was applied to obtain mechanically treated L-CNFs (ML-CNFs). The results show that mechanical treatment significantly improves the dispersion and individualization of L-CNFs, thereby enhancing fluid rheology and reducing filtration loss in BT-WBDFs. Salt and hot rolling influence the rheology and filtration performance of L-CNF/BT- and ML-CNF/BT-WBDFs differently. ML-CNF/BT-WBDFs exhibit greater resistance to salt contamination due to increased fibrillation and dispersed fibrils forming a more cohesive network in solution. In contrast, L-CNF/BT-WBDFs performed better under hot rolling due to reduced surface area and fewer exposed hydroxy groups. Nevertheless, the combined effects of salinity and elevated temperature strongly impact the rheological properties and filtration-control efficiency of both systems. Under the combined effects of salinity and elevated temperature conditions, ML-CNFs display superior resistance compared with L-CNFs. This improved performance is attributed to the more stable network structure of ML-CNFs, which promotes better dispersion of bentonite platelets under saline and high-temperature conditions, thereby enhancing system stability. Overall, the study highlights ML-CNFs as a promising additive for improving the performance and sustainability of water-based drilling fluids.

title: Advances in piezoelectric materials with diverse crystal structures: from design to applications
author: Yang, Danni
abstract: Piezoelectric materials are the cornerstone of modern electromechanical energy conversion, critical for advancing technologies ranging from sensors to precision actuators. While their performance is intrinsically linked to the piezoelectric coefficient, which dictates energy conversion efficiency and device sensitivity, optimizing this property remains a challenge due to the profound influence of diverse microscopic structures. This review comprehensively examines three fundamental crystalline architectures, namely perovskite, wurtzite, and fluorite, and critically analyzes performance optimization strategies tailored to each structure. We delve into five principal modification approaches, including defect engineering, elemental doping, heterostructure films fabrication, composite films design, and buffer layer incorporation, with a focus on elucidating the underlying physical mechanisms that govern property enhancements. By providing a cross-structural comparison of these strategies, this review establishes clear structure property relationships, offering a foundational guide for material selection and design. Furthermore, we highlight the implications of these advanced materials for next-generation applications in energy harvesting and smart devices. Finally, the review concludes with a forward-looking roadmap, outlining emerging research directions and addressing key technical challenges to guide the development of next-generation high-performance piezoelectric materials. 压电材料是现代机电能量转换的基石, 对于推动从传感器到精密执行器等技术的发展至关重要. 其性能本质上取决于决定能量转换效率与器件灵敏度的压电系数, 然而, 由于材料多样的微观结构对这一特性具有深远影响, 如何优化压电系数仍是一项挑战. 本综述系统梳理了三种基本晶体构型(钙钛矿型、 纤锌矿型与萤石型), 并深入评述了针对各结构量身定制的性能优化策略. 我们深入探讨了四种主要改性途径, 包括元素掺杂、 异质结构薄膜制备、 复合薄膜设计及缓冲层引入, 着重阐明了调控性能增强的物理机制. 通过对这些策略进行跨结构比较, 本综述建立了清晰的构效关系, 为材料选择与设计提供了基础性指导. 此外, 我们强调了这些先进材料对新一代能量采集与智能器件应用的重要意义. 最后, 本综述以展望性路线图作总结, 勾勒了新兴研究方向, 并针对关键技术挑战提出了应对思路, 以指导下一代高性能压电材料的开发.

title: Fly Ash Stabilization of Expansive Soils: Mechanisms, Engineering Properties, and Machine Learning Applications — A Comprehensive Review
author: Yadav, Navin Kumar
journal: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
abstract: Expansive soils represent a major challenge to civil engineering infrastructure because of their volumetric instability and poor engineering characteristics. This review is based on a systematic discussion of the way fly ash improves engineering properties of expansive soil. This study focuses on the fundamental behaviour of expansive soils in terms of their mineralogy, swelling phenomenon and engineering characteristics. The review summarises the contributions of studies on the improvements of engineering properties of significance such as Atterberg limits, compaction characteristics, strength parameters, volume change behaviour and hydraulic properties. The quantitative synthesis of data published in the literature indicates that optimum fly ash contents by weight typically range from 15 to 25% of most expansive soils and provide significant strength gain (UCS increase of 150–400%), huge reduction in swelling potential (reduction of 40–80%), and improved durability. SEM, XRD and other characterization techniques provide microstructural evidence of the physicochemical processes occurring during the process of stabilisation. The application of artificial intelligence and machine learning methods for prediction and optimization of stabilization outcomes is critically assessed as an emerging dimension of this field. The principal novelty of this review lies in the integration of a systematic quantitative synthesis of 87 published studies with mechanistic interpretation, providing statistically consolidated dosage–performance relationships and a unified framework that bridges fundamental soil chemistry, engineering practice, and computational modelling, an approach not adopted in previous reviews on this subject.

title: Enhancing foam production through surfactant synergistic effects: A review of current developments and future prospects
author: Rakam, Abhinay
abstract: This review paper provides a critical review of the synergistically interactive effects of binary surfactant mixtures in foam systems with regard to enhancing Foam Concrete (FC) and other industrial applications. The behaviour and the interactions of the surfactant molecules in a binary system are different from those observed in monophase systems. To understand these dynamics, this work analyses a mixture of surfactant combinations: non-ionic–cationic, non-ionic–anionic, cationic–anionic, and ionic–zwitterionic to investigate synergism and dynamics of surfactants and the resultant foam characteristics and performance. The result presented here suggests that the rates of drainage, foamability, and oil recovery improve when either non-ionic and anionic, or ionic and non-ionic, or both anionic and amphoteric surfactants are blended. The influence of combined surfactants over single surfactants shows that the enhancement in the system can be attributed to a decline in interfacial tension and lower critical micelle concentration (CMC) for various combinations, such as TX-100 + AOS, C_16TAB + C_18TAB, SDS + Triton X-100 + Tween 60 and CAPB + SDS. The proportional content and its composition, and hydrophilic or hydrophobic SiO_2-NPs, are characterised as vital parameters in creating the saving foam layers. It is not denied that with ‘synergistic blends’ of surfactant systems, the potential of these formulations to work in different applications is enhanced, as the review pointed out, especially on the importance of formulation on the efficacy of the intended system. This work proposes strategies for promoting advanced foam systems, particularly within FC technology, and outlines directions for future research and development.

title: Influence of chitosan incorporation on the thermo-mechanical, fatigue, creep, and flammability behavior of canabo fiber–reinforced epoxy composites
author: Gayathri, N.
abstract: This study presents the development and characterization of Canabo natural fiber (CNF)–chitosan–reinforced epoxy composites with an emphasis on their mechanical durability, creep behavior, thermal conductivity, and flammability performance. A systematic evaluation was carried out across different composite formulations to assess the influence of chitosan incorporation on overall material performance. Among the developed systems, the EF2 composite (40 vol% CNF + 3 vol% chitosan) exhibited the most balanced performance, showing improved fatigue resistance with 32,000 cycles at 25% UTS and 19,900 cycles at 75% UTS, along with the lowest recorded creep strain of 0.0021 at 1000 s, indicating enhanced resistance to time-dependent deformation. Thermal analysis indicated a thermal conductivity of 0.213 W/mK for EF2, reflecting improved heat transfer characteristics rather than insulation behavior. In terms of flammability, EF2 demonstrated superior performance with the lowest flame propagation speed (0.050 m/s) and highest limiting oxygen index (LOI) value of 29, indicating enhanced resistance to combustion. Morphological observations from SEM analysis suggest improved fiber–matrix interaction and more uniform fracture characteristics in the optimized formulation. Overall, the results demonstrate that the combined incorporation of CNF and chitosan leads to a multifunctional epoxy composite with improved fatigue life, creep resistance, and fire performance, making it a promising candidate for applications requiring enhanced structural reliability and flame resistance.

title: Multivariate optimization of uranium removal via radiation-grafted acrylonitrile/acrylamide polymers on hollow fibers with phosphonic functional group modifications
author: Alahyarizadeh, Ghasem
journal: Journal of Radioanalytical and Nuclear Chemistry
abstract: A novel polymeric adsorbent was prepared by gamma radiation-induced grafting of acrylonitrile and acrylamide onto polypropylene hollow fibers, followed by amidoximation and phosphonic acid functionalization. The adsorbent was characterized by FTIR, SEM, and TGA. Response surface methodology (CCD) optimized uranium adsorption: pH 4.9, 22.6 mg L^−1 U, 127 min, achieving 99% removal and adsorption capacity > 180 mg g^−1. Kinetics followed pseudo-second-order (R^2 = 0.999), and isotherms fitted Langmuir model. The phosphonic group enhanced selectivity and reusability (stable over 4 cycles). The adsorbent shows promise for uranium recovery from aqueous solutions.

title: Digital-Twin and IoT-Enabled Closed-Loop Dispatch for Dynamic Ore-Grade Blending in Open-Pit Mining
author: Uchkun, Eshonkulov
abstract: Open-pit mining operations are often plagued by mill feed variability and economic loss as a result of the difference between the static block models and the actual ore grade. Traditional truck dispatch systems are based on heuristic rules or open-loop optimization and cannot adjust for real-time grade fluctuations that are recognized during the extraction process. This paper proposes a novel closed-loop Digital Twin (DT) framework for dynamic ore blending and dispatch optimization by integrating Internet of Things (IoT) sensor streams with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). We propose a Residual Bayesian LSTM module to predict ore grades with uncertainty quantification from noisy sensor telemetry, enabling high-fidelity virtualization of the mining process. This digital twin is used to feed a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agent, which is trained using a multi-objective curriculum to make real-time dispatch decisions that balance production throughput and strict blending quality constraints. Validated on the MineLib benchmark under realistic sensor-noise scenarios, our framework outperforms industry-standard heuristics and open-loop Deep Q-Networks (DDQN). Experimental results indicate that the proposed system achieves a 22.3% target hit rate within a strict tolerance of ± 10%, a six-fold improvement over baseline heuristics (3.7%), and reduces mill feed grade variance by 38% in a simulated MineLib benchmark environment. Ablation studies also show that uncertainty quantification plays a critical role in stability, helping avoid risky dispatch decisions and reducing high-grading. These results demonstrate the feasibility of autonomous, uncertainty-aware, closed-loop control for increasing resource recovery and operational sustainability in Industry 4.0 mining.

title: Insects as a New Source of Biomolecules and their Application in Agroindustry, Cosmetics and Pharmacology
author: Joubari, Mariam El
abstract: This article highlights recent developments and the latest progress made in the use of insects as a new source of biomolecules in various fields like agro-industry, cosmetics and pharmacology. Indeed, numerous insect species such as the honeybee ( Apis mellifera ), the mealybug ( Coccus cacti ), the silkworm ( Bombyx mori ), the mealworm ( Tenebrio molitor ) and others constitute a rich source of bioactive molecules (enzymes, hormones, peptides, proteins, fatty acids, polysaccharides…) that can be used to develop innovative and effective products with various activities: antioxidant, antimicrobial, anticancer, anti-inflammatory, etc. The advantages and challenges associated with the use of insects as a source of biomolecules are also discussed. The article concludes by stressing the importance of further research into biomolecules of insect origin and their potential applications in a wide range of industries.

title: Domestic low temperature washing as a critical point in kitchen towel hygiene. Effectiveness of washing temperature, disinfectant and antibacterial finishing
author: Čuk, Nina
abstract: Background This study evaluated the efficacy of high- and low-temperature laundering, chemical disinfection, and antimicrobial textile finishes in reducing Bacillus cereus , Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, and Listeria monocytogenes on domestic kitchen towels. Results Polyester microfibre, cotton, and cotton/linen blend fabrics were experimentally inoculated and laundered with and without a commercial detergent at 60 °C–40 °C, treated with a commercial disinfectant, or subjected to an antibacterial finish. Laundering at 60 °C with detergent achieved reductions of more than 5 log₁₀ CFU/carrier for all tested bacteria, with complete reduction of S. enterica Typhimurium and L. monocytogenes across all textile types. In contrast, washing at 40 °C with detergent yielded reductions of less than 4 log₁₀ CFU/carrier and failed to effectively inactivate any of the target organisms, indicating that low-temperature laundering may constitute a significant reservoir for foodborne pathogens. Washing at 60 °C and 40 °C was less efficient than washing at a constant high temperature, indicating the combined effect of temperature and detergent. Both disinfectant treatments and the antimicrobial finish met established hygiene thresholds. Cross-contamination assessments revealed high bacterial transfer (more than 4 log₁₀ CFU/carrier) for all bacteria and textile types under baseline conditions, whereas laundering at 60 °C or applying the antimicrobial finish substantially reduced transfer. B. cereus, however, persisted following both mitigation approaches. Complete microbial inactivation on all textiles was achieved only with the addition of the disinfectant, underscoring its importance when lowering wash temperatures. Similar trends were observed in wash water: water from the 40 °C washing programme contained more than 4 log₁₀ CFU/mL, while water from the 60 °C washing programme and antimicrobial finishes limited survival primarily to B. cereus (detection limit 2.5 CFU/mL). The addition of disinfectant resulted in microbial reduction below the detection limit in wash water. Conclusions Overall, low-temperature domestic laundering of kitchen towels may facilitate the dissemination of foodborne pathogens. B. cereus emerged as the least susceptible strain to both thermal and chemical interventions. Therefore, reductions in domestic wash temperatures should be accompanied by effective chemical disinfection to prevent foodborne illness transmission. Graphical Abstract

title: One-step melt synthesis of Zn^2+-doped 2D manganese(II)-based coordination polymer phosphors
author: Lai, Yuhua
abstract: 通过简单、 可规模化的合成方法开发高效、 稳定、 低成本的荧光粉对于固态照明仍然至关重要。 本文开发了一种一步无溶剂法, 用于合成红色发射的Zn^2+掺杂锰基配位聚合物荧光粉Mn_1− x Zn_ x (OAc)_2 (OAc = 醋酸根)。 加热过程中, Mn(OAc)_2·4H_2O释放出的结晶水形成均匀的熔融相。 这一过程促进了具有八面体配位的无水Mn(OAc)_2的生成, 并有利于 Zn^2+的均匀掺入。 得益于优化的局域环境, Zn^2+掺杂 ( x =0.2) 有效抑制了与缺陷相关的非辐射衰减以及 Mn^2+ 之间的能量转移。 因此, Mn_0.8Zn_0.2(OAc)_2展现出高达 28.7% 的光致发光量子产率 (PLQY)、 1.03 ms 的寿命以及优异的热稳定性。 通过将该红色荧光粉与商用蓝、 黄荧光粉结合在紫外芯片上, 展示了 CIE 色坐标为 (0.34, 0.35) 的全光谱白光 LED。 这项工作为面向固态照明应用的高性能 Mn^2+ 基荧光粉提供了一种简便且可规模化的策略。 To address the challenges of complex preparation procedures, high organic solvent consumption, and poor environmental stability of products in conventional phosphor synthesis, this study proposes a simple, low-cost, solventfree one-step melt synthesis strategy, by which a series of Zn^2+-doped manganese-based coordination polymer phosphors, Mn_1− x Zn_ x (OAc)_2 (OAc=acetate), were prepared. During heating, Mn(OAc)_2·4H_2O releases its crystallization water to form a homogeneous molten phase, thereby yielding octahedrally coordinated anhydrous Mn(OAc)_2. Systematic investigations reveal that the optimal Zn^2+ doping concentration ( x =0.2) significantly enhances luminescence performance by suppressing defect-related non-radiative decay pathways and mitigating energy transfer between Mn^2+ ions. The optimized Mn_0.8Zn_0.2(OAc)_2 phosphor achieves a photoluminescence quantum yield of 28.7% and a lifetime of 1.03 ms, while its PL intensity at 140 °C is enhanced by 54% compared with Mn(OAc)_2, demonstrating excellent thermal stability. By integrating this red-emitting phosphor with commercial blue and yellow phosphors onto UV chips to fabricate full-spectrum white LEDs, ideal white light emission with CIE coordinates of (0.34, 0.35) is realized. This work provides a simple, environmentally benign, and scalable route for preparing high-performance Mn(II)-based coordination polymer phosphors for next-generation solid-state lighting applications.

title: Progress and Prospects in Cascade Upgrading of CO_2 Electroreduction Products Toward Long-Chain Chemicals
author: Ren, Houan
abstract: Electrocatalytic CO_2 reduction reaction (CO_2RR) has achieved remarkable selectivity toward C_1 and C_2 products; however, the direct electrosynthesis of long-chain (C_4+) and structurally complex molecules remains challenging. Coupling CO_2 electrolysis with downstream biological, thermal, electrochemical, or organic transformations offers a practical route to produce long-chain and structurally complex compounds, thereby expanding the product spectrum to include fuels, fine chemicals, polymers, and functional materials. In this mini review, we systematically summarize recent progress in four representative cascade configurations: electro–biological, electro–thermal, electro–electro, and electro–organic systems. For each configuration, we discuss the underlying principles, analyze the key coupling challenges, and summarize the corresponding optimization strategies along with representative studies. We further compare the technological features, product scope, and scalability limitations of these cascade systems in terms of reaction condition compatibility, multiphase interface engineering, energy efficiency, and system integration. Finally, we outline future research priorities aimed at accelerating the translation of CO_2 cascade technologies from laboratory-scale proof-of-concept studies to industrially relevant platforms.

title: ETS-guided iPSC-endothelial models recapitulate malaria pathogenesis
author: Korbmacher, François
abstract: This study benchmarks iPSC-derived endothelial models driven by the regulation of the ETS-transcription factors (ETV2, ERG and FLI1) and demonstrates their ability to recapitulate key pathogenic features of cerebral malaria in vitro. The sequestration of the malaria parasite in the microvasculature is a major driver of severe malaria, but the human specificity of Plasmodium falciparum has challenged our understanding of this key pathogenic process. Advances in induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) technologies offer unique opportunities to study parasite-host interactions in a well-defined environment. However, endothelial iPSC differentiation methods often result in cells with mixed epithelial identity. Here, we have generated an iPSC line with inducible and simultaneous expression of ETS transcription factors (ETV2, FLI1, ERG), resulting in cells with improved endothelial identity and strong barrier function (ETS-iBMEC). Parasite-infected red blood cells and neutrophils display high binding to ETS-iBMEC. Exposure to parasite products caused transcriptional changes in metabolic and splicing genes, and key endothelial barrier and angiogenic pathways. Our study confirms the role of the angiopoietin-Tie2 axis in parasite-mediated barrier disruption and highlights the importance of new pathways, including VEGF-Notch signalling. Our novel iPSC-based approach represents a new in vitro platform to study the pathogenesis of human vascular infections. This study benchmarks iPSC-derived endothelial models driven by the regulation of the ETS-transcription factors (ETV2, ERG and FLI1) and demonstrates their ability to recapitulate key pathogenic features of cerebral malaria in vitro. Endothelial identity was established through ETS transcription factor regulation during iPSC differentiation, as confirmed by transcriptomic and ultrastructural analyses. Enhanced barrier function was observed compared to primary brain endothelial cells, supporting suitability for modeling blood-brain barrier dysfunction in cerebral malaria. Key pathogenic events, including parasite accumulation, immune cell recruitment, and widespread endothelial responses, were recapitulated and partially reversed by pharmacological agents and recombinant protein supplementation. The platform enables application of iPSC-based advantages, including genetic modification and controlled host background, for in vitro malaria infection studies.

title: Kinetics of aggregation and hydrolysis of water-dispersible polyester in sodium hydroxide solution: processes and interaction mechanism
author: Wang, Jie
abstract: Water-dispersible polyester (WPET), as an amphiphilic macromolecule, shows significant value in textile sizing applications. However, in alkaline environments, WPET undergoes simultaneous aggregation and hydrolysis, complicating its removal during fabric processing. This study systematically investigates the aggregation and hydrolysis kinetics of WPET with varying -SO_3^- and PEG contents in NaOH solution, along with their interaction mechanisms. By combining DLS, zeta potential, fluorescence spectroscopy, alkali consumption measurements, and product characterization, the interplay between NaOH concentration and WPET molecular structure in regulating solution stability and phase transitions is elucidated. The addition of NaOH triggers a competition for water molecules between the ions and the WPET chains: the strong hydration of Na^+ and OH^- strips the hydration layer surrounding the sulfonate and PEG segments, exposing the hydrophobic backbones and leading to oligomer aggregation. This hydration‑layer evolution is the microscopic origin of the observed salting‑out effect. The conformational looseness of WPET chains, primarily governed by the sulfonate group content, serves as a key structural parameter: a more extended conformation facilitates NaOH penetration, thereby accelerating both aggregation and hydrolysis. NaOH concentration exhibits a critical threshold (approximately 0.2 M): below this concentration, hydrolysis predominates; above it, strong aggregation inhibits hydrolysis by forming dense aggregates that physically shield ester bonds. These findings provide a mechanistic guideline for practical textile desizing and alkali‑treatment processes, indicating that moderate rather than excessive alkali concentrations are more effective for WPET removal.

title: Mechanical and wear performance of polyethylene terephthalate glycol and carbon fiber 3D printed composite
author: Sravanthi, K.
abstract: The assessment of the mechanical properties and wear behavior of 3D-printed polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG) and carbon fibre (CF)-reinforced composite was established at different applied load and sliding speed. The present study investigates the individual effect of carbon fiber reinforcement on tensile, flexural, impact, hardness and wear test. Thermoplastic PETG reinforced with carbon fibers exhibits remarkable enhancement in terms of mechanical characteristics. This includes an amazing increase of 50% in tensile strength, 60% in flexural stiffness, and a 30% enhancement in impact resistance. Results of the wear testing showed that the coefficient of friction (CoF) as well as wear rate increased with increasing applied load and speed before reaching a plateau at high values, indicating the steady-state condition. A further reduction is evident at 90 mm/s (PETG-7 to PETG-9), where the CoF reaches its lowest range (≈ 0.40–0.44) with minimal standard deviation, reflecting stable sliding conditions and enhanced structural integrity. Findings from the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis indicated that the abrasive wear, adhesive wear, and fiber pull-out were the wear mechanisms involved. Fracture SEM validates the enhancement of stress transfer through the strengthening of fiber-matrix interfacial compatibility and the reduction of void formation in the PETG-carbon fiber 3D printed composite and EDX spectrum reveals the C/O system of reinforcement in carbon fiber PETG matrix. As the PETG-carbon fiber composites have shown suitable enhanced material properties, its potential applications can be in the fields where strength, durability, and resistance to wear are required. However, it can be improved by optimizing the 3D printing parameters. Graphical abstract

title: Additive manufacturing of advanced electronic devices: a comprehensive review of materials, processes, and applications
author: Karuniawan, Bayu Wiro
journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
abstract: The additive manufacturing (AM) technology has gained recognition as an innovative technology that holds promise for transforming the electronics industry through the realization of complex designs and multi-material integration. Advances in additive manufacturing (AM) technologies and materials are now paving the way towards novel electronics. This review paper focuses on the background, materials, and technologies that need to be considered for the fabrication of electronics using AM technology. The major AM processes, such as material extrusion, vat photopolymerization, material jetting, binder jetting, and powder bed fusion, provide specific design freedom and multi-material integration possibilities. On the other hand, improvements in conductive inks, dielectric polymers, and substrates have led to the widening of AM applications in areas like printed circuit boards, sensors, antennas, and energy storage devices. In addition to the specific topics of materials and technologies, this paper highlights the wide field of applications associated with AM electronics. Nevertheless, several problems arise in the way of wider implementation of these achievements, such as those related to material conductivity, resolution, interlayer adhesion, and standardization of the process. In order to tackle these problems, further research should be conducted on multi-material printing at the nanoscale level and the use of 4D intelligent materials for building adaptive and reconfigurable systems. Future development of AM technologies in electronics will include the incorporation of AI and IoT to provide quick, sustainable, and highly personalized devices. This review tries to bring together current progress and new prospects and show how AM technologies may change the face of electronics manufacturing.

title: Solvent-mediated tailoring of charge transport and dielectric behavior in APS-synthesized polypyrrole/carbon black nanocomposites
author: Ignasius, Haidy
journal: Journal of Materials Science: Materials in Electronics
abstract: Polypyrrole/carbon black (PPy/CB) composites were synthesized via in situ oxidative polymerization of pyrrole using ammonium persulfate (APS) in 1,2-dichlorobenzene. The influence of carbon black loading on the optical, structural, thermal, dielectric, and electrical transport properties of polypyrrole (PPy) was systematically investigated. UV–Vis spectroscopy revealed a gradual redshift in the absorption edge with increasing carbon black content, indicating modification of the local electronic environment. FTIR, Raman, and XPS analyses confirmed the successful incorporation of carbon black within the PPy matrix and suggested changes in local structural organization. SEM and HRTEM investigations revealed progressive morphological modification, heterogeneous aggregate formation, and close polymer–filler contact, while XRD patterns exhibited predominantly amorphous PPy features together with graphitic contributions from carbon black. Thermogravimetric analysis demonstrated improved thermal stability and increased char yield in the composites. Broadband dielectric spectroscopy revealed strong Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars interfacial polarization and non-Debye relaxation behavior, which was well described by the Havriliak–Negami model. AC conductivity followed Jonscher’s Power law, with σ_dc increasing from 5.67 × 10⁻^7 S/cm for pristine PPy to 1.54 × 10⁻^5 S/cm for the 8 wt% CB composite (CPA CB 80). Impedance spectroscopy and equivalent circuit analysis further indicated improved electronic connectivity and facilitated charge carrier movement upon carbon black incorporation. Overall, the results demonstrate that carbon black significantly influences the structural organization, thermal stability, dielectric response, and electrical transport behavior of PPy composites, providing insight into the design of conducting polymer composites with tunable electroactive properties.

title: Development and functional assessment of a polymer supported nanoscale iron hybrid for sustainable enhancement of water based drilling fluids
author: Jaf, Pshtiwan T.
abstract: Eco-friendly biopolymers in water-based drilling fluids often suffer from thermal degradation and inadequate filtration control under harsh downhole conditions. To overcome these limitations, this study aimed to develop a high-performance, sustainable hybrid nanocomposite that synergistically combines the structural resilience of biopolymers with the mechanical strength and pore-plugging capabilities of metallic nanoparticles. A ternary nanocomposite (IRON-NC) was synthesized via an in-situ reduction-stabilization method, embedding nanoscale zero-valent iron (nZVI) within a crosslinked chitosan and carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) matrix. The material’s morphology, chemical interactions, and electrokinetic properties were characterized, followed by comprehensive rheological and filtration evaluations under both standard and high-pressure/high-temperature (HPHT) conditions. Unlike standalone biopolymer additives, this hybrid architecture leveraged strong electrostatic repulsion (zeta potential of -48.5 mV) and robust polymer-metal bonding to ensure uniform dispersion and exceptional thermal reliability. At a remarkably low optimal dosage of 1000 ppm, IRON-NC induced pronounced shear-thinning behavior, increasing plastic viscosity to 37.6 cP and yield point to 13 Pa to ensure effective cuttings suspension. Furthermore, the nZVI-reinforced matrix facilitated the deposition of a highly compact, structurally resilient filter cake, reducing both API and HPHT fluid loss by 43–47% compared to the base fluid. The synergistic integration of nZVI with the chitosan-CMC network effectively resolves the thermal and mechanical vulnerabilities associated with conventional eco-friendly additives. Ultimately, IRON-NC presents a highly efficient, multifunctional, and environmentally compliant solution for improving rheology, stability, and fluid loss control in advanced drilling operations.

title: Integrated approaches for microplastic detection, risk assessment and sustainable biotechnological remediation
author: Prasad, Bhairav
abstract: Plastics have become indispensable in modern society, with extensive applications in electronics, transportation, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, packaging, and food systems. However, their widespread use has led to the emergence of microplastics (plastic particles ranging from 1 µm to 5 mm), which represent a pervasive and largely invisible form of environmental pollution. Due to their small size, persistence, and resistance to degradation, microplastics can evade conventional filtration systems and disperse widely through air, water, and soil. They have been detected in remote environments such as deep-sea sediments, high-altitude mountain regions, and Antarctica, indicating their global distribution and environmental persistence. Microplastics are distributed across terrestrial, aquatic, and atmospheric ecosystems and are transferred to higher trophic levels through food webs, resulting in reductions in soil microbiota, soil fertility, and ecosystem functioning. Rising evidence also associates microplastic exposure to adverse human health effects, including respiratory disorders, inflammation, oxidative stress, gastrointestinal disturbances, and potential carcinogenic risks. Recent advances in analytical techniques have improved the detection of microplastics in environmental and biological samples. Furthermore, emerging waste management strategies, microbial and biotechnological approaches, have promising potential for the degradation and remediation of microplastics. Overall, incorporating multidisciplinary strategies, including waste management, public awareness and scientific innovation, is essential to monitor, mitigate, and ultimately reduce microplastic pollution. Graphical abstract

title: Challenges and Prospects for the Manufacture of Polymer Liners for Hydrogen Composite Pressure Vessels: An Overview
author: Reda, Reham
journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
abstract: Hydrogen is a crucial energy carrier for decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors. Compressed hydrogen storage in composite pressure vessels is a viable solution for mobile applications. However, the polymer liner in Type IV composite pressure vessels is a significant technological bottleneck, limiting widespread hydrogen adoption due to design, material performance, interfacial integrity, industrial scalability, and reliability issues. However, advancements in self-healing polymers and nanocomposites could enhance barrier performance dramatically, alongside emerging 3D printing techniques promising scalability and cost-efficiency. Digital engineering and virtual “digital twins” enable rapid design and testing, facilitating the development of smart storage systems. Transformative approaches, including next-generation materials design, potentially scalable manufacturing processes, digital integration, and safety validation, are needed to overcome barriers in hydrogen storage technology. These approaches facilitate the development of lightweight, cost-effective, and durable pressure vessels, thereby supporting the advancement of the hydrogen economy and contributing to the achievement of global decarbonization targets. With the escalating global energy challenges and the fast-paced transition toward a hydrogen-based economy, urgent collaboration among industry, academia, and regulatory bodies is necessary to align innovation with climate goals and ensure sustainability throughout the process. By fostering partnerships and global collaboration, the polymer liner can be transformed into a breakthrough for hydrogen’s sustainable energy future. This review synthesizes the grand challenges, evaluates emerging solutions, and introduces a benchmarking framework. In addition, it outlines a roadmap for polymer liner deployment, identifies future research priorities, and highlights strategic opportunities.

title: Photothermal Superhydrophobic Textiles: An Emerging Paradigm from Passive Water Repellency to Active Thermal Management
author: Sheng, Tianyu
abstract: This review proposes a representative framework for photothermal superhydrophobic textiles, highlighting the transition from single-material studies toward integrated, system-level design and intelligent applications. This review deciphers the synergistic mechanism between photothermal conversion and superhydrophobicity, linking nano‑/micro‑scale material design to active de‑icing and self‑cleaning performance. This review critically analyzes scalable fabrication, real‑world applications, and key challenges, while outlining AI‑guided optimization and stimulus‑responsive systems as future pathways. Photothermal superhydrophobic textiles represent an emerging paradigm integrating active light-driven functionality with passive liquid repellency. While previous reviews treated superhydrophobicity and photothermal effects in isolation, this work pioneers a systematic analysis of their synergistic interplay—a critical, underexplored mechanism where superhydrophobicity preserves photothermal efficiency by minimizing water-induced heat loss, while photothermal activity prevents surface fouling that compromises non-wetting performance. Through detailed case studies of advanced material systems, this review highlights how this synergy supports significant advancements in adaptive wearable technology, energy-efficient infrastructure, and eco-friendly water treatment. This review presents an original “lab-to-life” roadmap that structurally links material design to durability assessment, environmental impact evaluation, and scalable manufacturing strategies—a holistic framework absent in existing literature. The review emphasizes urgent sustainability priorities including green material substitutions, non-toxic solvent processing methodologies, and circular design principles aligned with global environmental regulations. By connecting fundamental mechanisms to real-world deployment scenarios while outlining transformative future directions such as AI-accelerated material discovery, stimulus-responsive systems, and intelligent manufacturing protocols, this work provides a timely and actionable reference for advancing next-generation textiles toward technological sophistication and practical viability in sustainable development.

title: Materials–Structure–Hardware–Algorithm Co-Driven Hierarchical Optimization for Flexible Sensors
author: Zhu, Pengyu
abstract: Flexible electronics represent a paradigm shift in modern electronics, with flexible sensors serving as pivotal components in these systems. Despite significant advances driven by innovations in materials, structures, hardware, and algorithms, conventional design approaches that focus on optimizing individual hierarchies have inherent performance trade-offs, limiting further development. This review contends that future performance enhancements can no longer rely solely on breakthroughs in separate components. Still, it must adopt a new co-design paradigm spanning the “materials–structure–hardware–algorithm” hierarchy. In this review, we systematically organized the research landscape and representative advances across these four key hierarchies, analyzed the importance and recent breakthroughs in hierarchical synergy, and established a forward-looking theoretical framework to foster innovation and development in the field of flexible sensing. A novel co-design paradigm is proposed. A holistic co-design paradigm of “materials–structure–hardware–algorithm” is proposed here to overcome the performance trade-offs of traditional fragmented sensors. A systematic research framework is established based on the fundamental composition of flexible sensors. The interrelations within this dynamic field are clarified by structuring the review on the core hierarchies of materials, structure, hardware, and algorithms.
