title: CAF-derived exosomes inhibit ferroptosis via GALNT14-mediated O-GalNAcylation of SLC7A11 in colorectal cancer
author: Guan, Jialu
abstract: In the tumor microenvironment (TME), cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs)—the dominant stromal component—actively shape cancer progression through exosome-mediated communication. Here, we identify hsa_circ_0003892 (circLDLR ), a CAF-derived circRNA, as a key factor associated with poor prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC). During interactions between CAFs and CRC cells, circLDLR is packaged into exosomes and transferred to tumor cells, where it enhances proliferation and metastasis primarily by reducing susceptibility to ferroptosis. Mechanistically, circLDLR stabilizes Polypeptide N-Acetylgalactosaminyltransferase 14 (GALNT14) by protecting it from ZNRF2-mediated ubiquitination and degradation. This stabilization promotes the O-GalNAcylation of Solute Carrier Family 7 Member 11 (SLC7A11) at Ser26, facilitating its membrane localization and thereby suppressing ferroptosis in CRC cells. Additionally, we demonstrate that the RNA-binding protein EIF4A3 facilitates circLDLR biogenesis within CAFs. Taken together, our study reveals that CAF-derived circLDLR confers ferroptosis resistance and promotes CRC progression via the GALNT14/SLC7A11 axis. Consequently, disrupting exosomal circLDLR transfer between CAFs and CRC cells may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for CRC. Schematic diagram of the mechanism by which CAF-derived circLDLR promotes CRC progression through ferroptosis regulation. In the tumor microenvironment, CAFs highly express circLDLR , whose biogenesis is facilitated by EIF4A3-mediated splicing of LDLR pre-mRNA. circLDLR is then packaged into exosomes and transferred to CRC cells. Within CRC cells, circLDLR specifically binds to GALNT14 and inhibits its ubiquitination and degradation mediated by ZNRF2, thereby enhancing GALNT14 protein stability. Stabilized GALNT14 promotes O-GalNAcylation of SLC7A11 at Ser26, facilitating its membrane localization and increasing cystine uptake. The elevated cystine metabolism enhances GSH production, thereby suppressing ferroptosis and driving CRC cell proliferation and progression.

title: Micro-fibrillated lignocellulose films for high-performance sustainable packaging
author: Yeganeh, Fariba
abstract: Nanocellulosic materials, including nanofibers and microfibers, are promising sustainable alternatives for packaging due to their biodegradability, excellent film-forming ability, and robust mechanical performance. In this study, we produced microfibrillated lignocellulose (MFLC) from bleached chemithermomechanical aspen pulp using low-consistency refining (LCR) as a promising material for sustainable packaging. The MFLC was then converted into high-strength, water-resistant films with unique dual wettability—hydrophobic on one side and hydrophilic on the other—through casting, drying, and hot pressing. This opposing wettability naturally arises from the intrinsic hydrophobicity of lignin and its high interfacial energy with water, causing nano-lignin particles to accumulate at the film surface during formation. This feature provides promising potential for advanced packaging applications. Key packaging metrics—including mechanical strength, water vapor transmission rate, porosity, and thermal stability—were characterized. Increased thickness improved tensile strength and tear resistance, whereas hot pressing further improved tensile strength and thermal stability but reduced flexibility. These findings highlight MFLC produced though LCR as a promising precursor for bio-based packaging materials, particularly when high strength, thermal stability, and controlled surface hydrophilicity are required.

title: Tamarind seed xyloglucan: extraction technologies, structure–function relationships, and emerging applications in food, health and packaging systems
author: Pawase, Prashant Anil
abstract: Tamarind seed xyloglucan (TSX) is an underutilized, thermostable hemicellulosic polymer with remarkable functional and bioactive properties, attracting increasing research attention in recent years. This review presents a comprehensive overview of recent progress in sustainable extraction techniques, structure–function relationships, and versatile applications of TSX. Conventional and emerging extraction methods, such as hot water extraction, Soxhlet defatting, high-pressure processing, subcritical water extraction, microwave-assisted extraction, enzyme–ultrasound hybrid extraction, and irradiation techniques, are critically examined for their effects on yield, molecular weight, rheological behavior, solubility, and bioactivity. The polymer’s structural characteristics, including galactose-rich side chains, branching patterns, and molecular weight distribution, are discussed in relation to its shear-thinning, viscoelastic, gelling, emulsifying, and film-forming properties. Evidence from in-vitro and in-vivo studies demonstrates TSX’s prebiotic potential, production of short-chain fatty acids, anti-inflammatory activity, and metabolic benefits. Additionally, chemical and enzymatic modifications (such as OSA substitution and degalactosylation), along with composite formulations incorporating chitosan, proteins, and ZnO nanoparticles, have broadened its functional versatility. TSX shows promise as an ingredient for texture modification, cryoprotection, edible coatings, and targeted nutraceutical delivery. However, challenges remain regarding scalability, standardization, and regulatory validation. Future studies should emphasize green processing optimization, structure–function elucidation, and industrial translation to harness TSX’s potential as a sustainable functional biomaterial fully. Graphical abstract

title: Sustainable coal-PLA hybrid composite filament with closed-loop extrusion control: design, manufacturing, and life-cycle assessment
author: Sengottaiyan, M.
abstract: During the study presented, an experimental evaluation of a novel coal-reinforced PLA composite filament for load-bearing fused filament fabrication was conducted. The structure utilized was a novel type of composite filament made of coal particles as reinforcements in a type of plastic known as polylactic acid (PLA) that has been layered with other PLA outside materials on all sides. The new materials and method of making them were tested together to improve mechanical strength, printability, and environmental performance. In order to ensure the quality of the feedstock used in printing, a closed-loop extruder with real-time monitoring of filament diameter and PID control was developed, with a tolerance of ± 0.15 mm on both virgin and recycled polymer filament. Coal-filled PLA (20 wt%) achieved 28.1% higher tensile strength and 35.2% higher flexural strength than neat PLA, while closed-loop extrusion with real-time diameter monitoring held filament diameter within ± 0.15 mm and reduced defect rate from 18.3% to 3.2%. There was no modification to the surface finish or accuracy of the composite from the outside layer of PLA during mechanical testing. After the third cycle of recycling, the composite material retained 92.3% of its mechanical property testing results. Economic and life-cycle assessment indicate approximately 38–46% reduction in material cost and 42% reduction in carbon footprint compared with commercial virgin PLA feedstock. This new framework provides a way to cost-effectively and efficiently produce sustainable composite filament materials in a large-scale manner.

title: From waste to worth: Valorisation of Phyllanthus emblica L. fruit peel waste for pectin-derived edible coatings for apples
author: Thanta, Shefali
journal: Journal of Food Measurement and Characterization
abstract: Preharvest and postharvest factors have significantly affected apple supply chain across the globe. As an adaptation to the rising demand for apples and market trends for optimised profits, low-temperature storage and controlled atmosphere storage are used for extending the shelf life of apples. However, these storage facilities are limited in effectiveness. A promising alternative of edible coatings is gaining momentum in maintaining postharvest apple physiology. They maintain apple quality, reduce microbial load and control the gaseous exchange. This review provides a comprehensive overview of edible coatings on various perishable food produce, especially emphasising on different cultivars of apple. This work underscores the idea of synthesising edible coatings for apple from industrial processing by-products like Phyllanthus emblica (amla) fruit peel. The phytochemical profile, pharmacological importance, and postharvest challenges of amla fruit are discussed, opening new avenues for valorisation. It explores the novel idea of using amla peels to extract pectin and synthesise an edible coating. The work highlights pectin extraction techniques and its industrial potential. Postharvest apple preservation techniques are extensively reviewed, with an emphasis on edible coatings as a green packaging method and on promoting the circular economy. Graphical Abstract

title: A source-tailored engineering framework for methane bioconversion: from abatement infrastructure to biomanufacturing platforms
author: Hong, Hyo Jin
abstract: While methanotroph-based bioconversion is a promising solution for mitigating methane emissions, its industrialization remains constrained. This limitation stems from substantial physicochemical disparities among real-world emission sources, highlighting a profound disconnect between laboratory-scale achievements and practical operational barriers. To bridge this divide, this review proposes a comprehensive, source-tailored decision-making framework. For diffuse emissions, the energy deficits caused by large volumetric overheads mandate an energy-minimized abatement strategy. Conversely, centralized point sources offer strong concentration driving forces that justify capital-intensive, high-efficiency biomanufacturing platforms to maximize productivity. Furthermore, guided by techno-economic analysis, we diagnose specific engineering bottlenecks, confirming that process improvements must strictly align with distinct market profiles, ranging from bulk single-cell protein and mid-value polyhydroxyalkanoates to high-value ectoine. Finally, we outline how prospective research frontiers can disrupt current technological paradigms. Strain-process multiscale modeling resolves the critical scale-up hurdle, and digital twin-based verification systems translate measurement uncertainties into tradable carbon assets. Moreover, co-producing site-integrated bio-fertilizers via nitrogen fixation can transform low-concentration abatement infrastructures into self-sustaining models. Although tailored approaches are currently necessary, central to future transitions is utilizing ultra-low-level methane enrichment to converge diffuse capture with centralized biomanufacturing. Advancing this frontier could eventually enable a truly integrated, universal methane biorefinery. Source-tailored strategies bridge GHG mitigation and methane biorefineries. Energy-minimized abatement vs productivity-maximized manufacturing is contrasted. Engineering bottlenecks for ectoine, PHA, and SCP are diagnosed using TEA.

title: Effect of fully microbial-based nanocomposite film on the quality and shelf life of trout fillets
author: Baygar, Tuba
journal: Journal of Food Science and Technology
abstract: Microbial dextran from Leuconostoc mesenteroides and microbially synthesized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) via Streptomyces griseorubens were combined to form a nanocomposite film to evaluate their potential in prolonging the quality and shelf life of fresh rainbow trout ( Oncorhynchus mykiss ) fillets during refrigerated storage (4 ± 1 °C). In the control group, sensory acceptability dropped below the acceptable limit on day 12, while both coated groups remained at acceptable levels until day 18. When compared to the coated groups, the control group exceeded the acceptability limit for total volatile base nitrogen (TVB-N) (35 mg N/100 g) on day 18.TBA values increased from 0.17 to 0.72, 2.10, and 2.26 mg MDA/kg in groups K, A, and B, respectively, remaining well below the limit (8 mg/kg). Microbiological analysis revealed that the total mesophilic bacteria count reached the critical limit of 7 log CFU/g on day 8 in the control group, day 12 in group A, and day 16 in group B, showing an approximately 8-day extension of shelf life compared to the control group. The results indicated that the nanocomposite film effectively preserved the quality characteristics of the fish samples, extending their shelf life by approximately 6 to 8 days compared to the control groups. Graphical abstract

title: Engineering chitosan functionalized extracellular vesicles for targeted brain gene delivery and neurotherapeutics
author: Hashemi, Hawzhin
abstract: Gene therapy represents a crucial frontier in modern medicine for brain diseases; however, a significant obstacle hinders its progress. The immense difficulty of therapeutic molecules that deliver to the brain should be in a safe and effective way. The challenge is that blood brain barrier (BBB) blocks most drugs from entering. Exosomes offer a powerful solution to this problem due to their innate ability to cross this barrier and biocompatibility that makes them exceptional platforms for gene delivery. This article provides a detailed analysis of the latest methods for engineering these exosomes with a specific emphasis on chitosan. Chitosan possesses unique properties that can enhance exosome function. The authors introduce a clear framework to organize and understand this chitosan engineered exosomal systems. This framework categorizes them based on key features like their design architecture, the type of genetic cargo they carry, their specific targeting mechanisms and their stage of development toward clinical use. The review also offers a comparative analysis of preclinical animal studies to assess the therapeutic potential, limitations and progress of these systems toward human trials. It further covers innovative techniques that leverage chitosan to improve critical steps in the exosome workflow. These steps include the isolation and purification of exosomes, the efficient loading of drug/gene cargo and the precision targeting of brain tissue. Evidence from these preclinical models demonstrates that exosomes modified with chitosan achieve superior gene transfer efficiency and produce stronger neuroprotective outcomes compared to unmodified versions. This review outlines the current challenges that block the path to clinical applications. These challenges include scalable manufacturing and long-term safety studies. The goal is to advance chitosan based exosomal gene therapy from a promising concept into a viable and standardized treatment for a range of neurological diseases. Graphical Abstract

title: A comprehensive overview of the properties, applications, advancements, and safety of biodegradable packaging films
author: Singh, Sakshi
abstract: The growing environmental and regulatory concerns associated with synthetic plastic packaging have intensified research on biodegradable packaging films derived from renewable biopolymers. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the functional properties, applications, technological advancements, and safety considerations of biodegradable packaging films used in food packaging systems. This review integrates and evaluates the material design, performance metrics, and application-driven requirements within a single framework, which is directly aligned with the scope of sustainable food packaging. The mechanical strength, barrier performance, and structural properties are critically discussed in relation to formulation parameters such as polymer type, plasticization, blending, crosslinking, and nanofiller incorporation. Studies indicate tensile strength values ranging from approximately 0.7 to 32 MPa, elongation at break from about 1 to 370%, and water vapor permeability values in the range of ~ 10^–14 to 10^–9 g·m^−1·s^−1·Pa^−1. These performance ranges explain why biodegradable films are not yet replacements for conventional plastics but remain application-specific solutions. Consequently, their application in fresh produce, meat, dairy, bakery, and seafood packaging can extend shelf life and preserve quality for approximately 3–20 days. However, recent advancements like nanocomposites, multilayer structures, and active and intelligent packaging systems have expanded application while simultaneously raising concerns of food-contact safety, migration behavior, regulatory compliance, and end-of-life management. For biopolymer films, limited adoption is primarily due to moisture sensitivity, mechanical trade-offs, high production costs and scalability constraints. Therefore, contribution of biodegradable packaging to Sustainable Development Goals, particularly responsible consumption and production and climate action, is still limited.

title: Polymeric composites based on polyacrylic with polyethylene glycol and calcium chloride for atmospheric water harvesting
author: Martínez-Castillo, Carlos Aarón
abstract: Effective hygroscopic polymeric composites were developed for atmospheric water harvesting. Up to 1.49 g_moisture/g_composite moisture uptake and 1.09 g_water/g_composite self-released water at 90% RH. Simultaneous water absorption and release achieved without external energy input. Composite retained ~ 45% sorption capacity after 10 sorption–desorption cycles. Materials for Atmospheric Water Harvesting (AWH) have emerged as an alternative to address freshwater scarcity, which affects millions of people. Such materials are able to absorb moisture from the environment and can condense it without being near natural resources like rivers, lakes or oceans. In this study, polymeric composites have been synthesized using poly(acrylic acid) incorporating calcium chloride (CaCl_2) and polyethylene glycol (PEG) for efficient moisture absorption, condensation and self-water release. The obtained results show that it was possible to achieve a maximum moisture absorption of 1.49 g_moisture/g_composite in 12 h at 90% relative humidity and simultaneous spontaneous water release of 73% (1.09 g_water/g_composite) without external heating. In addition, the composite remained functional along several days of study in outdoor analysis and released 0.23 g_moisture/g_composite despite environmental fluctuations. FTIR analysis confirmed the integration of PEG and CaCl₂, while DSC results indicated thermal stability at room temperature. The composite maintained 44% of its initial absorption capacity after ten sorption-desorption cycles.

title: Nanocarrier strategies to enhance oral bioavailability of plant-derived bioactives
author: Bouzidi, Amal
journal: Journal of Food Measurement and Characterization
abstract: Bioactive compounds from natural sources such as polyphenols, carotenoids, flavonoids, and other phytochemicals play pivotal roles in modulating oxidative stress, inflammation, and metabolic homeostasis, thereby contributing to disease prevention and overall health promotion. However, their clinical and nutritional effectiveness is constrained by poor aqueous solubility, chemical and enzymatic instability, and rapid first-pass metabolism, which collectively result in low systemic bioavailability. Conventional enhancement approaches, including structural modification, emulsification, and co-administration with lipid carriers, have yielded only marginal improvements. In contrast, nanoparticle-based delivery systems have emerged as a versatile platform capable of simultaneously overcoming multiple physicochemical and biological barriers. Nanoscale encapsulation enhances solubility, protects against degradation, improves mucosal adhesion and intestinal transport, and enables controlled or site-specific release within the gastrointestinal tract. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of the mechanistic principles governing nanoparticle-mediated enhancement of bioavailability, a comparative overview of major nanocarrier systems, and their applications in functional foods and nutraceuticals. Furthermore, it discusses current progress in safety evaluation, regulatory frameworks, and consumer acceptance, and outlines emerging directions toward smart, targeted, and sustainable nutritional nanotechnology platforms. Graphical abstract Nanocarrier-based delivery systems improve the oral bioavailability of plant-derived bioactive compounds by overcoming physiological and biochemical barriers through enhanced solubility, protection from degradation, improved intestinal absorption, and controlled release, ultimately supporting functional food and nutraceutical applications

title: Photodynamic anti-biofilm PHEMA/Rose Bengal hydrogels enhanced by iodide: evidence for hydrogen peroxide and triiodide formation
author: López-Fernández, Ana M.
abstract: Biofilm-associated infections remain a major challenge for biomedical devices, motivating the development of light-activated antimicrobial materials. Here we report the antibiofilm activity (against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ) of a photodynamic hydrogel consisting of Rose Bengal (RB) physically entrapped within a crosslinked poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate) (PHEMA) matrix. Under visible-light irradiation, RB-PHEMA alone produced only modest reductions (ca. 1 log), whereas addition of iodide markedly enhanced antibiofilm performance, yielding a 4.2-log reduction for S. aureus and a 1.7-log reduction for P. aeruginosa . To elucidate the basis of iodide potentiation, we conducted a systematic spectroscopic study under irradiation with varying concentrations of KI and NaI. Long-lived products consistent with iodide oxidation by singlet oxygen were detected, including triiodide (I_3^−) and hydrogen peroxide (H_2O_2). I_3^− was observed within the PHEMA hydrogel but not in the supernatant, consistent with electrostatic retention in the polymer network, while H_2O_2 was detected both at the hydrogel surface and in the surrounding solution, indicating diffusion away from the material. These findings support a mechanism in which diffusible H_2O_2, together with polymer-retained iodine species, contributes to biofilm inactivation beyond short-lived reactive intermediates. Practically, 10 mM iodide was sufficient to reach the maximum I_3^− signal, and NaI performed comparably to KI. The transparency and flexibility of the hydrogel support applications requiring conformal contact and back-illumination. Finally, photobleaching of RB within the hydrogel is effectively eliminated in the presence of iodide, providing an additional practical advantage of iodide as a potentiating additive.

title: Nano-enabled pesticides in woody plants: route-fit delivery, in planta fate, and evidence standards for sustainable pest control
author: Li, Min
abstract: Forestry pesticide delivery is often inefficient: canopy sprays and bark treatments suffer from drift, rainfall wash-off, and photolysis, and many important pests and pathogens occupy concealed woody habitats that are hard to reach. Nano-enabled formulations can improve deposition, weathering resistance, and controlled release, but their value in woody plants depends on route-specific anatomy and on whether intact carriers or released payloads drive in planta redistribution. We develop a route-fit framework linking formulation design (carrier chemistry, architecture, and triggerability) to the main delivery routes in woody systems (foliar, bark/interface, trunk injection, and soil/root) and to measurable endpoints relevant to pest control (dose efficiency, rainfastness, persistence, and systemic reach). We synthesize evidence across carrier families and target niches, explain why fluorescence-only imaging can mislead in autofluorescent lignified tissues, and outline orthogonal strategies (e.g., tracer-enabled mass balance and isotopic/elemental approaches) to separate intact-carrier fate from payload transport. We then translate these insights into field-ready metrics, scale-up considerations, and decision rules to prioritize formulations that reduce total pesticide inputs and off-target losses while maintaining durable suppression of forestry pests and pathogens.

title: Borneol-based nanoparticles encapsulating Doxorubicin/Sodium tanshinone IIA sulfonate enhance the effect of anti-glioma and alleviate cardiotoxicity
author: Ye, Xiaoli
abstract: Clinical treatment of brain glioma remains challenging due to chemotherapeutic resistance, cardiotoxicity and the presence of blood-brain barrier (BBB). Advanced nanoplatforms that can cross the BBB efficiently and target brain glioma with lower cardiotoxicity are urgently needed. Herein, the protective effect of borneol-based nanoparticles encapsulating Doxorubicin/Sodium tanshinone IIA sulfonate (BO-Dox/STS-NPs) on glioma was explored. BO-Dox/STS-NPs were comprehensively evaluated by measuring their particle size, encapsulation efficiency, and drug-loading capacity. Pharmacokinetic studies evaluated their concentrations in animal serum and brain. In an orthotopic rat glioma model, the antitumor efficacy and cardioprotective effects of Dox, Dox/STS, Dox/STS-NPs, BO-Dox/STS-NPs, and Dox-NPs were compared. In vitro, U87 cells were treated with these formulations, and antitumor effects were assessed via CCK8 assay, flow cytometry, migration assay, and colony formation assay. In orthotopic glioma rat models, treatment with BO-Dox/STS-NPs resulted in superior tumor inhibition and increased tumor cell apoptosis compared to other formulations. Furthermore, BO-Dox/STS-NPs significantly alleviated doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity, as evidenced by improved myocardial pathology, reduced left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and decreased levels of cardiac injury markers (cTnI, CK) and oxidative stress indicators (LDH, MDA), alongside enhanced antioxidant capacity (SOD) and mitochondrial membrane potential. In vitro, BO-Dox/STS-NPs exhibited the greatest uptake of Dox, the strongest inhibitory effects on U87 cell proliferation, migration, and colony formation, and promoted apoptosis more effectively than other treatment groups. Co-loading Dox and STS into borneol-modified nanoparticles enables effective treatment of glioma while reducing cardiotoxicity. This approach contributes to the development of a versatile technological platform for constructing diverse brain-targeted nanocarriers.

title: DREAMS illuminates spatial DNA and RNA modification landscapes
author: Peng, Yan
abstract: DNA and RNA modifications regulate gene expression and RNA processing, but their spatial organization in complex tissues remains elusive. Here we developed DNA RNA Elements Areal Mass Spectrometry (DREAMS), a mass spectrometry imaging platform that spatially maps diverse nucleic acid modifications simultaneously. Applying DREAMS to TET-deficient mouse brains ( Tet1 ^ Δ/Δ and triple Tet1/2/3 ^ Δ/Δ ), we uncover TET1’s unexpected role in modulating N^1-methyladenosine (m^1A), a pivotal RNA modification. While DREAMS reveals broad modification landscapes altered across TET knockouts, we identify TET1-mediated changes in m^1A that correlate with transcriptome alterations. Our work establishes DREAMS as a transformative tool for spatial epigenomics/epitranscriptomics and suggests that TET enzymes could influence multiple DNA and RNA modifications with potential gatekeeping roles in nucleic acid regulation. Peng, Xue et al. develop a nucleic acid metabolites detection method, DNA RNA Elements Areal Mass Spectrometry (DREAMS) which enables the identification of DNA and RNA modifications, as well as spatial mapping of these modifications within tissues.

title: Bioinspired high refractive index of violet-emitting polycarbonate films doped with naphthalimide dye for luminescent solar concentrator windows
author: Alyami, Mohammed
abstract: Highly transparent, photostable, violet-emitting polycarbonate (PC) films doped with a naphthalimide dye (KREMER 94730) were fabricated by solvent casting at thicknesses of about 500 ± 5 μm. The aggregation onset was qualitatively assessed by X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy, which indicated uniform molecular dispersion of the dye up to 1.5 wt% and the formation of dye-clustered nanodomains at higher concentrations. The films exhibit strong UV–vis absorption and violet–blue fluorescence with a peak maximum around 440 nm and a quantum yield of 84% at 1.5 wt%, with CIE 1931 chromaticity coordinates of (x, y) ≈ (0.17, 0.05). Tauc and Ravindra–Penn analyses indicated bandgap narrowing from 4.0 to 2.97 eV and a corresponding refractive-index enhancement from 1.58 for pristine PC to 2.23 at 3 wt% dye loading, surpassing the high-refractive-index biopolymer chitin taken as a natural reference material for light confinement. These films are promising low-cost, sustainable matrices for luminescent solar concentrator windows in UV-rich environments, supporting daylighting and energy-efficient façades, and enabling climate-resilient building envelopes supporting urban SDG targets for clean energy and sustainable cities. Graphical abstract

title: Hydrophilic, hydrophobic, and porous nanosilica as green additives for geotechnical engineering in cold regions
author: Hamidi, Salaheddin
abstract: Freeze-thaw (F-T) cycles in cold regions severely degrade clay soils, leading to reduced strength, increased permeability, and compromised infrastructure stability. While conventional stabilizers like cement and lime are effective, their use is associated with high CO₂ emissions and resource depletion, raising environmental concerns. This study investigates nanosilica (NS) as a sustainable alternative for soil stabilization under F-T conditions. The research specifically evaluates the performance of three distinct nanosilica types—hydrophilic (HPI), hydrophobic (HPO), and porous (P)—with an average particle size of 20–30 nm—to determine how surface chemistry and morphology influence geotechnical behavior. Natural clay samples were treated with 0.5%, 1%, and 1.5% NS and subjected to up to 12 F-T cycles. Unconfined compressive strength (UCS), shear strength, permeability, and microstructural changes were analyzed using UCS, direct shear, falling-head permeability, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) tests. The findings reveal that the optimal choice of nanosilica depends on the engineering objective and exposure to F-T cycles. Under non-freezing conditions, 1% HPI-NS yielded the highest UCS (1.21 MPa, ~ 6.7× higher than untreated clay) due to extensive viscous gel formation. However, after multiple F-T cycles, 1% P-NS demonstrated superior durability (UCS = 0.95 MPa), attributed to nano-whisker development and enhanced matrix resilience. In contrast, 1% HPO-NS produced the lowest permeability across all conditions, owing to its water-repellent nature. SEM images confirmed gel formation and microstructural densification in treated samples. This study provides the first comparative framework for selecting nanosilica type based on application-specific goals—strength enhancement (HPI/P-NS) or permeability control (HPO-NS)—under realistic cold-region conditions. It highlights the potential of nanomaterials as environmentally responsible solutions for resilient geotechnical engineering.

title: Fabrication and performance of CA-PK-PVP membrane for oil-in-water emulsion separation
author: Arshad, Syed Khizer
abstract: The increasing global demand for clean water and the limitations of conventional wastewater treatment technologies have accelerated interest in sustainable membrane-based solutions. In this study, a novel cellulose acetate-poly ketone-polyvinylpyrrolidone (CA-PK-PVP) composite membrane was fabricated through a non-solvent induced phase separation (NIPS) method. The uniqueness of this work lies in the combined use of cellulose acetate as a hydrophilic biopolymer, poly ketone as a mechanically reinforcing and solvent-resistant component, and PVP as a hydrophilic pore-forming agent to tune membrane morphology and separation performance. Different CA: PK ratios (9:1, 8:2, 7:3 and 5:5) were first investigated, and the CA_8-PK_2 membrane showed the best balance between permeability and oil rejection. Further incorporation of PVP significantly enhanced membrane porosity and surface hydrophilicity, leading to the formation of an asymmetric porous structure with improved water transport pathways. The optimized CA_8-PK_2-PVP_5 membrane exhibited a low water contact angle of 42.3° and a high oil contact angle of 124.7°, indicating excellent hydrophilic and oleophobic surface properties. In addition, the membrane showed improved mechanical strength of approximately 23 MPa and good solvent resistance after long-term immersion in ethanol, hexane, isopropanol, and toluene. Among all fabricated membranes, CA_8-PK_2-PVP_5 achieved the optimal separation performance, with a high water flux of 848 L m⁻² h⁻¹ and oil rejection above 99% under a low operating pressure of 100 mbar. The membrane also effectively separated different oil-in-water emulsions, including hexane, toluene, xylene, and petroleum ether, while maintaining stable rejection performance over repeated filtration cycles. These findings demonstrate that the synergistic integration of CA, PK, and PVP provides an effective strategy for preparing high-performance membranes for oily wastewater treatment.

title: Review: MXenes for energy storage and conversion devices—advances in green synthesis, use of machine-learning, and electrochemical response
author: Opia, Anthony Chukwunonso
abstract: Recently, MXenes have become effective electrode materials for devices including batteries, supercapacitors (SCs), sensors, antennas, and optoelectronic devices, as well as for sustainable energy storage. They are promising choices for a variety of energy conversion and storage materials due to their metallic conductivity, good hydrophilicity, and ability to act as ideal templates for developing other materials with tunable features. Recent advances in energy devices and storage using MXene as electrode materials are outlined in this article. The fundamental ideas of energy storage and renovation systems are examined. The following sections highlight the special qualities of Green Synthesis Methods for MXenes. Potential fixes for issues that arose during the development of MXene were investigated, as was the use of Machine learning techniques as cutting-edge approaches to MXene product optimisation. Additionally, MXene's applications in energy conversion devices, such as supercapacitors, catalysis, various batteries, and electrochemical sensing were highlighted. A discussion of potential future opportunities for MXene-based materials in energy industries for sustainable technology wraps up the study.

title: Ultrasonic-Assisted Synthesis of a Gellan/PAA-ZIF-8 Nanocomposite Hydrogel for Efficient Heavy Metals Removal
author: Nemati, Maryam
journal: Journal of Inorganic and Organometallic Polymers and Materials
abstract: In this study, a novel and effective nanocomposite hydrogel based on gellan gum (GG) was created using polyacrylic acid (PAA) and zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) (GG-g-PAA/ZIF-8), which was successfully produced through a sustainable ultrasonic-assisted method. The combination of biopolymer gellan and crystalline ZIF-8 was designed to leverage its hydrophilicity, biocompatibility, and high surface area for the effective removal of toxic heavy metal ions. Comprehensive characterization using FTIR, XRD, and EDS confirmed the successful synthesis of the hydrogel, the efficient integration of ZIF-8 into its structure, and the formation of a porous, semi-crystalline, and thermally stable hybrid network. The synthesized GG-g-PAA/ZIF-8 hydrogel exhibited a swelling ratio of about 1078.8%, a compressive yield of 77.3 MPa, and contained uniformly dispersed ZIF-8 polyhedral particles within the gellan network surface. The GG-g-PAA/ZIF-8 hydrogel was used to remove heavy metal ions (Cd^2+, Pb^2+, and Ni^2+) from water via batch adsorption. Its efficiency depended on pH, and modeling showed a Langmuir isotherm and pseudo-first-order kinetics. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed the process was spontaneous and exothermic. Ultrasonic irradiation improved the dispersion and interaction of ZIF-8 within the gellan network, thereby enhancing adsorption capacity and structural stability. These findings suggest that the GG-g-PAA/ZIF-8 nanocomposite hydrogel is a promising, eco-friendly, and mechanically robust adsorbent for removing heavy metals from contaminated water.

title: Influence of CNT on the mechanical properties of FDM processed PLA nanocomposites
author: Managuli, Sangamesh C.
journal: Journal of The Institution of Engineers (India): Series D
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM), particularly stereolithography (SLA), has revolutionized polymer composite fabrication by enabling high-resolution, geometrically complex components. However, conventional UV-curable resins used in SLA processes often suffer from inadequate mechanical performance, limiting their application in load-bearing and high-wear environments. This study investigates the synthesis of polymer composites with improved mechanical properties by incorporating Titanium Carbide (TiC) particles into a photopolymer resin matrix. SLA was used to create composites with different TiC weight percentages (0%, 0.25%, 0.5%, and 0.75%) under ideal processing circumstances. In compliance with ASTM guidelines, the manufactured samples were assessed for mechanical performance, including tensile strength, flexural strength, impact strength and Shore D hardness tests. According to the results, the mechanical properties consistently improve as the TiC content rises. Compared to the unreinforced resin, the 0.75 weight percent TiC composite showed the greatest improvements, increasing its tensile strength by 50%, flexural strength by 73%, and Shore D hardness by 58.8%. The mechanical results were supported by SEM analysis of fracture surfaces, confirming improved interfacial bonding and efficient stress transfer mechanisms by revealing a shift from brittle to ductile failure modes.

title: Development of a Marine Algae-based Facial Cream Enriched With Phycoerythrin: Physicochemical Properties and Biological Activities
author: Kadalmani, Sowmiya
abstract: Phycoerythrin (PE), a marine phycobiliprotein derived from Hypnea valentiae , was extracted, characterized, and evaluated for its potential application in a topical cosmeceutical formulation. The extraction yielded 6.35 mg/g (wet biomass), and spectral analysis confirmed pigment integrity. PE exhibited strong antioxidant activity, with DPPH radical scavenging increasing from 32.4% to 78.6% (20–100 µg/mL) and an IC₅₀ of 46.8 µg/mL, while the ABTS assay showed an IC₅₀ of 41.3 µg/mL. Anti-inflammatory activity revealed IC₅₀ values of 52.1 µg/mL (PE extract) and 60.5 µg/mL (PE cream), compared to 46.6 µg/mL for diclofenac sodium. Antimicrobial analysis demonstrated concentration-dependent activity. HV-PE showed moderate inhibition, whereas the PE-infused cream exhibited enhanced efficacy, with zones of inhibition up to 1.77 cm ( Staphylococcus aureus ), 1.81 cm ( Bacillus subtilis ), 1.96 cm ( Escherichia coli ), and 2.11 cm ( Staphylococcus epidermidis ) at 1000 µg/mL. MIC/MBC values further confirmed improved antibacterial performance of the cream (e.g., S. aureus : 52.34/46.21 µg/mL) compared to HV-PE. The formulated cream showed suitable physicochemical properties, with pH 7.12 (control: 7.48) and improved spreadability (80.71 g·cm/s vs. 74.79 g·cm/s). The SPF increased from 12.08 (control) to 24.04 (PE cream). Zebrafish toxicity studies indicated no observable adverse effects, confirming biocompatibility. Overall, PE demonstrates significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and photoprotective properties, supporting its application as a multifunctional cosmeceutical ingredient. title: Binder Jetting of Fe-50Ni Complex Cores for Enhanced Soft Magnetic Performance
author: Soylemez, Emrecan
abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing offers efficient material usage and enables customized shape designs that are difficult to achieve with conventional methods. This study investigates the binder jetting of Fe-50Ni soft magnetic alloys, which are widely used in transformers, inductors, and motors due to their high flux saturation. The process evaluation focuses on the final densities and magnetic properties of both bulk and complex toroidal designs. Two Fe-50Ni powders with different particle size distributions were processed and sintered under both atmospheric and vacuum conditions. Sintering temperatures near 1360 °C enabled near-full densification, whereas 1335 °C produced geometrically stable parts for complex designs with ~ 80% density, suitable for toroidal inductors. Magnetic characterization showed that binder-jetted bulk toroid samples reached saturation flux densities comparable to a commercial reference at 50 Hz but exhibited broader hysteresis loops due to eddy current loss. In contrast, complex geometries incorporating cavities and segmented designs provided clear benefits, with concentric square-ring designs achieving the highest permeability and highest inductance up to ~ 7 kHz. These results confirm the feasibility of binder jetting for producing Fe-50Ni soft magnetic cores and highlight the potential of geometry-based design strategies to mitigate core losses and enable advanced electrical and electronic applications. title: Lignin-Assisted NiO Nanocomposite Electrode for High-Performance Supercapacitors: Structural Insights and Charge Storage Mechanism
author: Deniz, Ali Rıza
journal: Journal of Inorganic and Organometallic Polymers and Materials
abstract: The development of sustainable electrode materials requires the integration of renewable components without compromising electrochemical kinetics or structural durability. Herein, a NiO/lignin nanocomposite was prepared through lignin-assisted hydrothermal synthesis followed by thermal treatment at 350 °C. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed the formation of cubic NiO crystallites within a thermally transformed lignin-derived matrix containing residual aromatic and oxygen-bearing functionalities. The composite exhibited an average particle size of approximately 33 nm, a BET surface area of 86.4 m^2 g^−1, a total pore volume of 0.31 cm^3 g^−1, and a mesopore diameter centred at approximately 8.7 nm. The higher surface area and pore volume relative to pristine NiO support the structure-regulating effect of lignin incorporation. Electrochemical performance was evaluated in 1 M KOH using a three-electrode configuration, with pristine NiO and pristine lignin electrodes examined under identical fabrication and testing conditions. The NiO/lignin electrode delivered a specific capacitance of 812 F g^−1 at 1 A g^−1 and retained 74.1% of this value at 20 A g^−1. Its equivalent series and charge-transfer resistances were 0.82 and 3.35 Ω, respectively, indicating reduced ohmic losses and facilitated interfacial charge transfer. The anodic and cathodic b-values of 0.84 and 0.79, together with the Dunn analysis, revealed a mixed charge-storage mechanism involving surface-controlled and diffusion-dependent Faradaic contributions. Moreover, the electrode retained 94.2% of its initial capacitance with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.1% after 5000 cycles. The combined structural, kinetic, and control-electrode results indicate that NiO provides the primary Ni^2+/Ni^3+ redox sites, whereas the lignin-derived matrix improves particle dispersion, electrolyte accessibility, interfacial transport, and cycling stability. These findings establish the NiO/lignin nanocomposite as a promising electrode material while recognizing that its practical device performance requires further validation in a mass-balanced two-electrode configuration.

title: Cellular assemblies as living therapeutics
author: Gaspar, Vítor M.
abstract: Multicellular assemblies can be programmed to exhibit emergent behaviours that make them promising therapeutic tools, particularly for tissue regeneration and immunomodulation. This Review outlines the design principles, biological advantages and translational requirements for engineering hierarchical cellular assemblies with programmable functions and emphasizes the need for benchmarking them against single-cell and biomaterial-based approaches. Multicellular assemblies can sense and respond to biochemical and biophysical cues. They can also self-regulate and self-organize, giving rise to emergent behaviours over time. These features make cellular assemblies interesting therapeutic tools for applications such as tissue regeneration and immunomodulation. In this Review, we discuss the design space for therapeutic cellular assemblies, outlining hierarchical building blocks, including single cells and linear, planar and volumetric units, as well as physical and biological toolboxes for their fabrication and functional programming. We examine the biological features of hierarchical cell assemblies, analysing their potential therapeutic benefits, when benchmarked in relation to free-cell suspensions and dispersed cells delivered in biomaterials. Finally, we highlight applications of cellular assemblies in regenerative medicine, immunomodulation and production of biological mediators and discuss translational considerations, including scalable manufacturing, longitudinal characterization and predictive modelling approaches required to engineer cellular assemblies with programmable biological functions. Multicellular assemblies exhibit emergent, collective behaviours, such as coordinated sensing, self-regulation and self-organization, which make them fundamentally distinct from single-cell therapies. Therapeutic cellular assemblies can be engineered at multiple hierarchical levels, ranging from individual cells to linear, planar and volumetric units, using both biological and physical fabrication toolkits. Programming cellular assemblies enables tailored biological functions, leveraging control over cell–cell interactions, tissue-like organization and dynamic responses to microenvironmental cues. Hierarchical cell assemblies can provide therapeutic benefits, but benchmarking against free-cell suspensions or dispersed cells delivered in biomaterials is key to evaluating their performance. Successful clinical translation will require scalable biomanufacturing, robust longitudinal characterization and predictive modelling, ensuring reliable design and function of programmable cellular assemblies.

title: Characteristics of femtosecond laser-induced micro-nano topological structures on 7075 aluminum alloy surface
author: Li, Si
abstract: A single-step femtosecond laser processing strategy was employed to induce two-tier micro-nano topological structures on the surface of 7075 aluminum alloy, and their effects on surface wettability, surface hardness, and dry sliding tribological behavior were investigated. The laser-induced composite structure, consisting of micrometer-scale papillae and nanoscale laser-induced periodic surface structures, reduces the actual contact area between water droplets and the substrate while promoting the adsorption of hydrocarbon species, thereby imparting hydrophobic properties. A maximum static contact angle of 164° was achieved, with a sliding angle of 2.7° and a contact angle hysteresis of 7°, reaching a superhydrophobic state. Furthermore, the micro-nano structured surface demonstrated good hydrophobic durability during abrasive impact tests. The experimental results confirm that the femtosecond laser-induced micro-nano structures increase the surface hardness by up to 39% compared to the untreated sample. The grooves within the micro-nano structures can trap wear debris generated during sliding, mitigating abrasive wear. Compared to the untreated surface, the coefficient of friction and wear rate of the laser-treated surfaces were reduced by up to 29% and 44%, respectively. This study provides a feasible pathway for tailoring the wettability and durability of 7075 aluminum alloy surfaces using femtosecond laser micro-nano fabrication, demonstrating potential applications in aerospace, marine equipment, and other related fields.

title: Fabrication of Carbon Quantum Dot-Embedded Polymer Hydrogel Beads for Efficient Dye and Iodine Removal from Wastewater
author: Tadmadge, Rutuja B.
abstract: The release of persistent and dangerous dyes into aquatic environments poses significant hazards to human health and ecosystems due to their toxicity and resistance to adsorption. In this research, a novel composite adsorbent composed of polycarbazole (PCB) and carbon quantum dots (CQDs) encapsulated within sodium alginate (SA) beads (SA@CQD/PCB) was successfully synthesized and applied to remove dyes [direct black (DB), methylene violet (MV) and basic Victoria blue (BVB)] as well as iodine (I_2) from aqueous solutions. Initial dye concentrations of 50 ppm for MV, BVB, and DB and 200 ppm for I_2 were used in adsorption tests, achieving maximum removal efficiencies of 99.25%, 95.07%, 86.98%, and 86.37%, respectively. The superior adsorption performance is attributed to the synergistic interaction between CQDs and PCB, which provides abundant active sites for interactions and promotes π–π interactions. Kinetic studies revealed that the adsorption process followed the pseudo-second-order kinetic model (R^2 = 0.9995), indicating chemisorption as the dominant adsorption mechanism. The Langmuir isotherm analysis revealed a maximum monolayer adsorption capacity of 479 mg/gm for MV, demonstrating the excellent adsorption performance of the SA@CQD/PCB hydrogel beads. Furthermore, the practical potential of SA@CQD/PCB beads for large-scale wastewater treatment could be investigated in future studies to assess the feasibility of scaling up the adsorption process. All things considered, this work demonstrates the efficacy of adsorption-based techniques using sustainable composite materials for the removal of both cationic and anionic contaminant dyes, as well as I_2, from contaminated water. title: Formulation and In vitro Characterization of Rosuvastatin Calcium Loaded Chitosan Nanoparticles for Sustained Drug Release
author: Sarwer, Muhammad Umer
abstract: Rosuvastatin calcium (RST) is a BCS class II antihyperlipidemic drug with poor aqueous solubility, which limits its oral performance. The present study aimed to develop and characterize RST-loaded chitosan nanoparticles (CTS-NPs) using the ionic gelation method to improve physicochemical properties and achieve sustained drug release. Nanoparticles were prepared using chitosan and sodium tripolyphosphate (TPP) as a cross-linking agent via ionic gelation and were evaluated for particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, morphology, drug loading, entrapment efficiency, and in vitro drug release behavior. The optimized formulation exhibited a nanosized particle diameter of approximately 243.7 nm with a positive zeta potential of about + 30 mV, indicating good colloidal stability. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed spherical and uniformly distributed nanoparticles. Entrapment efficiency ranged from 65.80% to 93.08%, depending on formulation composition. FTIR, DSC, and XRD analyses confirmed successful drug incorporation without chemical incompatibility and revealed partial amorphization of RST within the polymeric matrix. In vitro release studies demonstrated an initial burst followed by sustained drug release up to 24 h, best fitting the Higuchi kinetic model, indicating diffusion-controlled release. These findings suggest that RST-loaded chitosan nanoparticles represent a promising oral nanocarrier system with sustained release characteristics and the potential to improve the oral performance of poorly water-soluble drugs such as rosuvastatin calcium.

title: Molten salt–assisted thermoelectric conversion of biomass for high-capacitance carbon materials
author: Ji, Deqiang
abstract: The growing global energy crisis and increasing greenhouse gas emissions necessitate the development of sustainable energy technologies. However, existing methods for synthesizing biomass-derived carbon materials suffer from limitations such as poor conductivity during low-temperature carbonization, high energy consumption during high-temperature activation, and the need for corrosive reagents, resulting in suboptimal electrochemical performance of the carbon materials. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel composite thermoelectric dual-field electrochemical technology that converts lignin into high-capacitance carbon materials under low-temperature conditions (550 ℃). Using alkali lignin and poplar leaves as raw materials, the products obtained through pyrolysis (2 h) and electrolysis (4 h, 2.8 V) exhibited specific surface areas of 286 and 388 m^2 g^− 1, respectively. In a three-electrode system, the specific capacitance at a current density of 0.5 A g^− 1 reached 230 and 177 F g^− 1; at a current density of 0.1 A g^− 1, the specific capacitance reached 343 and 270 F g^− 1. Furthermore, the resulting materials exhibited excellent rate capability and cycling stability; after 5,000 charge-discharge cycles in a 6 M KOH aqueous solution at a current density of 5 A g^− 1, the capacitance retention rates reached 99.6% and 99.5%, respectively. This molten salt-assisted thermoelectric dual-field method provides a new approach for the low-temperature, efficient preparation of porous carbon materials for biomass-based supercapacitors. Graphical Abstract

title: Rice Protein as an Alternative Ingredient for Sustainable Food Formulations: Nutritional Quality, Functional Properties, Health-promoting Potential, and Emerging Applications
author: Meza, Silvia Leticia Rivero
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable and nutritionally adequate protein sources has intensified interest in alternative plant proteins capable of supporting future food systems. However, many conventional plant proteins still present limitations related to allergenicity, digestibility, sensory quality, and functional performance, highlighting the need for novel sustainable ingredients. In this context, rice protein has emerged as a promising alternative due to its hypoallergenic nature, gluten-free composition, relatively high digestibility, suitability for specialized dietary applications, favorable techno-functional characteristics, and compatibility with sustainable food production systems. This review provides an integrated perspective on rice protein by critically discussing its nutritional quality, techno-functional properties, health-promoting potential, emerging food applications, and contribution to sustainable food systems, thereby addressing knowledge that has remained fragmented across previous reviews. Recent scientific studies addressing protein composition, digestibility, bioactive peptides, processing technologies, and applications in plant-based foods and nutraceutical systems were critically analyzed. Current evidence demonstrated that rice proteins and rice-derived peptides exhibit antioxidant, antihypertensive, anti-inflammatory, antidiabetic, and immunomodulatory activities, while recent advances in protein modification technologies have significantly improved solubility, emulsification, gelation, and structuring properties. Furthermore, the valorization of rice bran and broken rice supports circular economy strategies and sustainable food production. In this way, rice protein represents a strategic ingredient for the development of next-generation functional foods and sustainable health-oriented dietary systems.

title: Ligand-independent EPHA2 signaling sustains neural progenitors via ECSIT and NAD^+
author: Diem Nghi, Tran
abstract: EPHA2 sustains embryonic cortical progenitors by coupling apical receptor signaling to ECSIT-dependent Complex I activity and mitochondrial NAD^+, providing a functional link between cell surface receptor state and mitochondrial redox control during corticogenesis. Ligand-independent EPHA2 signaling is required for cortical progenitor maintenance in vivo. EPHA2 perturbation reduces mitochondrial respiration, Complex I activity, NAD^+ regeneration, and mitochondrial ECSIT abundance. Restoring mitochondrial NAD^+ regeneration or mitochondrial ECSIT attenuates progenitor defects caused by EPHA2 disruption. A PP2A-sensitive ECSIT phospho-state, including T179, links EPHA2 signaling to mitochondrial ECSIT accumulation. Embryonic neural stem and progenitor cells occupy a specialized niche along the lateral ventricles, where receptors on their apical membrane sense extracellular cues essential for preserving progenitor identity. How such surface signals are coupled to mitochondrial metabolism remains unclear. Here, we identify EPHA2 as a receptor enriched in cortical progenitors and show that disruption of its non-canonical, ligand-independent signaling compromises progenitor maintenance in vivo. EPHA2 perturbation reduces mitochondrial respiration, Complex I activity, and mitochondrial NAD^+ regeneration, and is accompanied by lower mitochondrial abundance of the Complex I assembly factor ECSIT. Restoring mitochondrial NAD^+ regeneration with MTS- Lb NOX, or restoring mitochondrial ECSIT with ECSIT WT—but not a mitochondrial targeting-deficient mutant—attenuates the progenitor defects caused by EPHA2 perturbation. Maternal supplementation with NAD^+ or its precursor NMN similarly mitigates these developmental defects. We further identify a PP2A-sensitive ECSIT phospho-state, including T179, that is consistent with regulated mitochondrial ECSIT accumulation downstream of EPHA2. Together, these findings support a model in which EPHA2 helps maintain embryonic cortical progenitors by sustaining ECSIT-dependent Complex I-linked mitochondrial redox homeostasis. EPHA2 sustains embryonic cortical progenitors by coupling apical receptor signaling to ECSIT-dependent Complex I activity and mitochondrial NAD^+, providing a functional link between cell surface receptor state and mitochondrial redox control during corticogenesis.

title: Dextran-based biodegradable film reinforced with glycerol and isomalto-oligosaccharides: characterization and preservation performance on strawberry
author: Zhang, Yao
journal: Journal of Food Measurement and Characterization
abstract: Microbially derived polysaccharides have attracted considerable attention for developing sustainable bio-based food packaging materials. In this study, a dextran-based composite film (DGI) incorporating glycerol and isomalto-oligosaccharides was fabricated and characterized. The DGI film exhibited improved mechanics with an elongation at bread of 44.17 ± 3.08% and tensile strength of 5.40 ± 2.60 MPa. It also showed favorable water vapor permeability ((46.94 ± 2.78) ×10^− 11 g·m/(m²·s·Pa)), high light transmittance and water solubility. Scanning electron microscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and thermogravimetric analyses confirmed its excellent molecular compatibility and enhanced thermal stability. During strawberry storage, the DGI film outperformed commercial polyethylene film in preserving quality, as evidenced by a more intact appearance, brighter color, and higher firmness. It also effectively inhibited the losses of in soluble solids, organic acids, and ascorbic acid, while delaying visible mold development. This study provides a theoretical basis and technical support for the applications of dextran-based biodegradable films in fruit preservation. Graphical abstract  An eco-friendly biodegradable film (DGI) was fabricated using dextran, glycerol, and isomalto-oligosaccharides (IMO); The DGI film exhibited desirable mechanical and barrier abilities, with good molecular compatibility and thermal stability; The DGI film outperformed commercial polyethylene film in preserving the quality of fresh strawberries.

title: Fish skin–derived collagen–chitosan composite membranes: Structure, properties, and packaging performance
author: Dang, Nhan Thi Thanh
abstract: Type I collagen was successfully extracted from catfish skin and blended with chitosan to form composite membranes. Intermolecular interactions between collagen and chitosan governed the microstructure and thermal stability of the composites. Composite membranes exhibited improved water resistance and antibacterial functionality compared with neat collagen. The optimized membrane demonstrated effective moisture barrier performance under refrigerated storage conditions. Sustainable and bio-based polymer materials are increasingly investigated as alternatives to synthetic plastics. In this study, type I collagen was extracted from catfish ( Pangasius bocourti ) skin, a seafood processing byproduct, and blended with chitosan to fabricate collagen–chitosan composite membranes. The structure and properties of the membranes were systematically characterized in terms of morphology, intermolecular interactions, thermal stability, water resistance, and antibacterial functionality. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed composition-dependent microstructural features, while Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) indicated intermolecular interactions between collagen and chitosan chains. The composite membranes exhibited enhanced thermal stability and reduced water solubility with increasing structural compatibility. The functional performance of the optimized membrane was further evaluated using persimmons ( Diospyros kaki ) as a model system under refrigerated storage conditions, demonstrating reduced moisture loss and delayed visible deterioration compared with unwrapped controls. The results illustrate how structure–property relationships govern the functional behavior of collagen–chitosan composites and highlight the potential of fish skin–derived collagen as a sustainable biopolymer resource.

title: Laser-induced surface texturing and nanomaterial functionalization of PLA/PHBV surfaces for enhanced cell adhesion
author: Queiroz, Rafaela Campos
abstract: Current research on the development of biomaterials aims at reducing bacterial colonization and increasing cell adhesion on the surface of implantable devices for regenerative medicine. Equally noteworthy is the growing interest in using materials from renewable sources and biodegradable in medical devices. In this study, femtosecond laser surface texturing was applied to PLA/PHBV polymer blends nanocomposites with and without cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) fillings. Micro-pillar structures were developed using a femtosecond laser. The textured samples were characterized by SEM, profilometry, and contact angle measurements. The effect of texturing on cytotoxicity, cell adhesion and proliferation were evaluated by MTT assay and confocal fluorescence microscopy by using L929 fibroblasts cell line. The results showed that laser texturing led to a significant increase in surface roughness and caused the material to change from hydrophilic to hydrophobic behavior, a phenomenon explained by the Wenzel model. The polymers showed higher cell viability and directional growth after laser treatment, especially in the samples containing 0.5–1.5 wt% CNT and up to 5 wt% CNC. However, it was observed that at high concentrations of nanofillers the biocompatibility was compromised, which could be attributed to particle agglomeration and percolation effects. Overall, this study highlights the synergistic role of laser-induced microstructures and functionalization with nanomaterials in modulating the surface properties of biopolymers to promote biocompatibility, offering a promising approach for the development of bioactive surfaces for high-performance implants.

title: Advances In the Valorization of Avocado By-Products: Bioactive Compounds, Techno-Functional Properties, and Structure–Function Relationships
author: Perucini-Avendaño, Madeleine
abstract: Avocado ( Persea americana Mill.) processing generates large amounts of peel and seed that remain underutilized despite their potential as functional food ingredients. While previous reviews have focused mainly on the chemical composition and antioxidant capacity of avocado by-products, less attention has given to the role of tissue-specific microstructure and ripening-related structural changes in determining their techno-functional behavior. This review critically integrates recent advances in the valorization of avocado by-products, with particular emphasis on peel and seed as sources of bioactive compounds and techno-functional ingredients. It examines the chemical composition, microstructural organization, and physicochemical transformations of these by-products, highlighting how their structural features influence functional performance. Special attention is given to phenolic compounds, dietary fiber, and associated polysaccharides, and to how cell wall architecture, pectin solubilization, and tissue disassembly influence the techno-functional properties of ingredients obtained from avocado by-products. These properties, such as water- and oil-holding capacities, emulsifying properties, and gelation behavior, are primarily evaluated after processing the by-products into functional food ingredients. Additionally, the review discusses the impact of processing and extraction strategies on structural integrity, bioactive retention, and techno-functional functionality, as well as recent advances in food-grade applications, bioaccessibility, safety considerations, and current challenges for industrial implementation. Overall, this review provides an integrated framework that links composition, microstructure, processing, and functionality to support the sustainable valorization of avocado by-products as value-added food ingredients.

title: Sustainable Avocado Seed Starch Nanoparticles for Limonene Encapsulation: A Novel Immunomodulatory Delivery System
author: Alves, Guilherme L.
journal: Journal of Polymers and the Environment
abstract: D-limonene is a bioactive monoterpene with recognized antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, whose therapeutic application is severely constrained by its high volatility, sensitivity to oxidation, and poor aqueous solubility. Nanoencapsulation within biopolymeric matrices represents a promising strategy to overcome these limitations. Therefore, this study aimed to develop and characterize chemically modified avocado seed ( Persea americana Miller) starch nanoparticles, produced via a simple one-step nanoprecipitation method, for D-limonene encapsulation, evaluating their physicochemical properties, long-term stability, and immunomodulatory potential. Acetylation of the starch was confirmed by FTIR, ¹³C NMR, and degree of substitution (DS) determination, which collectively demonstrated successful introduction of acetyl groups into the polymer backbone and the resulting increase in hydrophobicity that underlies the encapsulation capacity of the nanocarrier. Thermogravimetric analysis further characterized the physicochemical properties of the modified starch and nanoparticles. The resulting nanoparticles displayed mean diameters lower than 350 nm, predominantly homogeneous size distributions (PdI < 0.3), zeta potentials ranging from − 10.46 to − 13.77 mV and encapsulation efficiency higher than 80% in two formulations. Long-term stability assessment demonstrated preservation of colloidal integrity after 10 months under refrigerated storage, with retention of approximately 69% of initial encapsulation efficiency. TEM analysis revealed small, globular particles with smooth surfaces and narrow size distribution, while FT-IR spectroscopy provided surface chemistry characterization consistent with limonene confinement within the nanoparticle core. In vitro release studies demonstrated a sustained, gradual release profile, with 59.1% of the encapsulated DL released after 24 h and release kinetics best described by a first-order model, with Fickian diffusion as the dominant transport mechanism. Immunological analysis demonstrated a potent and context-dependent immunomodulatory potential of ASNP-DL1. In vitro assays showed the suppression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-6) in macrophages and dendritic cells, concurrently maintaining anti-inflammatory IL-10 at basal levels, indicating a coordinated shift toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. These findings underscore the potential of this sustainable nanocarrier as a versatile platform that effectively addresses the physicochemical limitations of D-limonene, positioning this sustainable, agriculturally-derived nanocarrier as a promising candidate for immunomodulatory therapies with broad pharmaceutical and biotechnological relevance.

title: Catechol modified sodium alginate/gelatin films reinforced with bio-mediated HNTs for enhanced wound healing applications
author: Ambrose, Anishia
abstract: The increasing prevalence of wounds caused by various causes that can cause complications in the everyday activities of humans is a significant worldwide health issue. Despite recent progress, there remains a substantial demand for efficient wound healing materials, especially for persistent and challenging wounds. The objective of the present work is to design a feasible, viable and efficient wound healing material. Sodium Alginate (SA) has been adopted for its remarkable cell viability and effectiveness in promoting wound healing. It is modified using catechol to enhance cell adhesion and to improve healing. Catechol modified sodium alginate is then blended with gelatin and leucas aspera leaf extract coated halloysite nano tubes (HNT). Leucas aspera is chosen for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. The Modified-HNT@catechol-SA/gelatin film is formulated by adopting the solvent casting technique. The resultant films were characterized for functional group changes using FT-IR, crystallinity by XRD, elemental composition by XPS, thermal stability via TGA and hydrophilicity and swelling ratio. The Modified-HNT@catechol-SA/gelatin film showed higher ZOI of about 18 mm and 19 mm against E. coli and S. aureus , antioxidant and anti-inflammatory potential (> 50%), MTT assay showed > 90% of cell viability against L929 cell lines and in-vitro scratch assay revealed 89.5  ±  1.27% of wound closure using L929 cell lines. Based on the findings, it is evident that the developed polymeric nanocomposite thin film will be considered for wound healing applications. Furthermore, the implementation in in-vivo wound healing studies is essential for the validation of the material in clinical applications.

title: Galactomannans from Neltuma spp. as Emerging Functional Dietary Fibre for Human Nutrition: Extraction Technologies and Health Potential
author: Escobar, Adrián
abstract: Galactomannans are reserve polysaccharides widely distributed in legume seeds and recognized for their technological and physiological properties. Their structure, consisting of a β-(1→4)-linked mannose backbone with α-(1→6)-galactose side chains, determines their solubility, viscosity, and functional behavior. In recent years, galactomannans have gained increasing attention as functional dietary fibre due to their potential effects on glycemic regulation, cholesterol reduction, gut microbiota modulation, and short-chain fatty acid production. This review critically analyzes the current knowledge on galactomannans derived from Neltuma spp., a group of underutilized leguminous species native to arid and semi-arid regions of Latin America, particularly the Gran Chaco ecosystem. This review aims to describe the structural characteristics of sources of galactomannans from seeds, extraction and purification technologies, and their potential nutritional implications of Neltuma spp.-derived galactomannans, highlighting their role as sustainable ingredients for human nutrition. Conventional extraction methods, including aqueous and alkaline extraction, are compared with biotechnological approaches such as enzymatic pretreatments, ultrasound-assisted extraction, and membrane technologies, highlighting their effects on yield, purity, and structural preservation. Evidence suggests that Neltuma spp. seeds represent a promising alternative source of food-grade galactomannans with potential applications as sustainable hydrocolloids and functional ingredients. However, studies regarding their digestibility, microbiota interactions, and clinical effects remain limited. The valorization of Neltuma spp. may contribute to the diversification of dietary fibre sources while supporting sustainable bioeconomy strategies and regional food innovation in Latin America.

title: Next-generation photodynamic cancer therapy: purpurin-based nanocarriers as emerging photosensitizers
author: Dudhwala, Yash D.
abstract: Cancer remains a leading global health burden, with approximately 20 million new cases and 9.7 million deaths reported in 2022, and projections indicating a substantial rise by 2050. Nearly one in five individuals is expected to develop cancer during their lifetime, underscoring the urgent need for more effective and targeted therapies. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has emerged as a minimally invasive modality that utilizes photosensitizers, light, and oxygen to generate cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) for localized tumor destruction. However, conventional photosensitizers are limited by poor solubility, low tumor selectivity, and suboptimal photostability. This review critically examines purpurin-18 and related chlorin-based nanocarriers as next-generation photosensitizer systems for PDT. Although their names are similar, purpurin-18 is chemically distinct from natural anthraquinone purpurin and is classified as a chlorin-type tetrapyrrolic macrocycle. Due to its red-light absorption, ROS-generating capacity, and chemical modifiability, purpurin-18 has shown improved therapeutic potential when incorporated into nanocarrier systems. Nanocarrier engineering significantly improves photosensitizer dispersibility, stability, and tumor targeting, enabling enhanced intracellular uptake and apoptosis induction across multiple cancer models. Despite promising preclinical outcomes, challenges related to safety, biodistribution, standardized photophysical characterization, and clinical translation persist. Future directions include the development of stimuli-responsive systems, combinatorial therapeutic strategies, and AI-assisted nanocarrier optimization to advance purpurin-18-based nano-PDT toward clinical applicability. Graphical Abstract

title: Haemodynamic control of zonated liver function via instructive vascular Wnt signalling
author: Lee, Ki Hong
abstract: The study identified blood flow as the key signal that programs liver blood vessels to instruct liver function through WNT signalling. The vascular endothelium forms a systemically disseminated organ that translates micromilieu factors into instructive cues, designated as angiocrine signalling. While vascular control of organ function mechanisms have been discovered in essentially all major organs, the mechanisms of translating milieu factors into angiocrine signalling mechanisms remain largely elusive. Here, focussing on the well-established angiocrine Wnt signalling-regulated liver metabolic zonation paradigm, we identified blood flow-induced haemodynamic stress as a biophysical sensor that governs the angiocrine expression profile of liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSEC). Combining single-cell RNA sequencing with spatial proteomics, we generated a high-resolution crosstalk map of LSEC and hepatocytes from LSEC Wnt-deficient mutant mice and littermate controls. Intriguingly, vascular Wnt receptors, in parallel with angiocrine Wnt ligands, were specifically enriched in pericentral LSEC, enforcing the spatially coordinated vascular Wnt functions. Consequently, vascular Wnt further modulated angiocrine gene signatures, LSEC morphology, and the expression of gap junctional molecules in an autocrine manner. Taken together, the data define LSEC as a dynamic cellular decoder that translates biophysical forces into instructive angiocrine signals via activating promiscuous vascular Wnt factors.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Optimization of Calcium Pectinate Hydrogel Formulations: A Stacked Ensemble Framework for Alpha-Lipoic Acid–β-Cyclodextrin Oral Delivery System Design
author: Raj, Karikalachsozhan Prakash
abstract: Background Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a major complication of diabetes mellitus, affecting nearly 30–50% of diabetic patients worldwide. Although α-Lipoic acid (ALA) demonstrates significant antioxidant potential in DPN management, its clinical application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, photochemical instability, and variable oral bioavailability. Complexation with β-cyclodextrin (βCD) may improve these physicochemical limitations; however, optimization of calcium pectinate hydrogel carriers remains challenging due to complex concentration-dependent interactions. Objective This study aimed to develop a stacked ensemble machine learning (ML) framework for predicting critical quality attributes of calcium pectinate hydrogels and to apply the model for rational design of an ALA–βCD oral delivery system. Methods A meta-dataset containing 91 formulation data points was curated from 10 peer-reviewed studies on calcium pectinate hydrogels. Fourteen engineered physicochemical features were derived from pectin and CaCl₂ concentrations. A leakage-free stacked ensemble comprising artificial neural network (ANN), random forest (RF), and XGBoost base learners with a Ridge regression meta-learner was evaluated using nested 5-fold cross-validation and pseudo-external validation. Virtual screening of 10,000 candidate formulations was conducted using the Derringer–Suich desirability function. FTIR spectroscopy and in silico ADMET profiling were performed to characterise the ALA–βCD inclusion complex. Results The stacked ensemble achieved cross-validated R² values of 0.93 for hardness, 0.91 for drug content, and 0.87 for T80, outperforming all baseline models. Pseudo-external validation confirmed satisfactory generalisation (mean R² = 0.89). SHAP analysis identified the egg-box stoichiometric ratio and crosslinking density index as dominant predictors of gel hardness. Virtual screening identified an optimal formulation region at pectin 5.7–6.4% w/v and CaCl₂ 1.5–2.0% w/v. FTIR confirmed successful ALA–βCD inclusion complex formation, while ADMET analysis demonstrated favorable oral drug-likeness and safety characteristics. Conclusion The proposed ML framework provides a robust and physically interpretable strategy for calcium pectinate formulation optimization and establishes a computationally guided foundation for ALA–βCD oral delivery system development.

title: Prognostic factors and predictive modeling of in-hospital mortality among MDRO-positive inpatients: a retrospective cohort and GBD MICROBE study
author: Jiang, Fan
abstract: Existing studies on prognostic prediction for multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) are limited by single-model designs, incomplete consideration of ward environmental observations, and insufficient linkage to national antimicrobial-resistance burden data.
